Michael A. Wilkins Michael A. Wilkins Talk Title: “ Awaken to Arise ” INTRODUCTION: In today’s rapidly evolving organizational landscape, leaders and entrepreneurs are challenged to achieve sustainable growth while maintaining clarity, culture, and performance. The concept of transformational leadership extends beyond strategy alone—it requires intentional mindset expansion, purpose- driven action, and measurable execution. Moments explores how deliberate leadership choices and aligned behaviors can create meaningful and lasting transformation at both individual and organizational levels. AIM: The aim of this presentation is to challenge leaders, entrepreneurs, and organizations to rethink their approach to growth, culture, and performance. It seeks to demonstrate that when individuals expand their mindset and align their actions with purpose-driven strategy, transformation becomes not only achievable but measurable. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This presentation employs a blended methodology that integrates practical leadership frameworks, real-world case studies, and evidence-informed mindset-shifting principles to support meaningful and sustainable transformation. The approach is highly interactive, incorporating guided reflective questions that promote self-awareness, strategic thinking, and intentional decision-making. Structured strategic models are introduced to help participants clarify priorities, align values with action, and translate vision into executable plans. In addition, participants engage with actionable tools and practical exercises designed to bridge the gap between ideation and implementation. These tools enable leaders to apply insights in real time, reinforcing learning through application and accountability. The methodology places strong emphasis on clarity, ownership, and measurable outcomes, ensuring that change is not conceptual but operationalized. Overall, the approach supports sustainable change through a step-by-step strategic alignment process that strengthens individual leadership capacity, enhances organizational effectiveness, and embeds continuous development into daily practice. RESULTS: Participants gain enhanced leadership capacity, improved organizational clarity, and the ability to cultivate high-performance mindsets within their teams. Attendees are equipped with practical tools to bridge the gap between vision and execution, enabling measurable progress in organizational culture, strategic outcomes, and personal development. CONCLUSION: This presentation reinforces the core belief that growth is not accidental but intentionally engineered through aligned thought, purposeful action, and continuous development. When individuals and organizations commit to mindset expansion, process strengthening, and clarity-driven leadership, they not only exceed expectations but establish new standards of excellence. KEYWORDS: Leadership development; mindset transformation; organizational growth; performance management; strategic alignment; purpose-driven leadership. Biography: Michael A. Wilkins is the Owner and Founder of Doage Consulting LLC, established in October 2025. He brings over 25 years of distinguished service in Washington State Government, where he has been a trailblazer in Program and Project Management. His work has focused on driving operational transformation, strengthening accountability, and enhancing public trust through efficient, transparent, and results-driven systems. Michael has provided leadership across numerous advisory boards and committees, including serving as Chair of the Fife Police Department Citizen’s Advisory Committee (2019–2024), Local Planning Area committees across Kitsap, South King, and Pierce Counties (2006–2017), McGregory Park and Saddle Creek Housing Developments, and Chair of the Sound Transit ADA Committee (2006–2024). He is also a Certified Motivational Speaker, international TEDx speaker, consultant, author, pastor, coach, musician, and certified trainer. Certified Motivational Speaker, International TEDx Speaker, consultant, Author, Keynote Speaker, Pastor, coach, musician and certified trainer.

Donna Reiners Donna Reiners Talk Title: “TRANSFORM from Within: Trusting the Voice Inside” INTRODUCTION: Many women leaders live outwardly successful lives while inwardly navigating noise, anxiety, performance pressure, and fragmented self-identity. Despite spiritual seeking and personal growth efforts, a gap often remains between daily lived experience and one’s truest, most aligned self. This keynote addresses that gap by reframing transformation not as effort or self-improvement, but as remembrance of truth, identity, and the Christ consciousness already present within. AIM: The primary aim of this session is to support participants in reconnecting with their inner truth and learning how to live from divine-centered alignment rather than emotional survival. Participants will explore how embodied spiritual awareness strengthens emotional regulation, self-trust, and congruent leadership rooted in authenticity, clarity, and inner guidance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this keynote, Donna Reiners introduces her proprietary TRANSFORM Method, a Spirit-led, faith-anchored framework designed to guide individuals from emotional survival into divine-centered alignment. Drawing on Christ consciousness (the Voice inside) as an awakened state of being rather than a religious construct, the method integrates hypnosis and Donna’s Christ Quantum Toolkit, which includes stillness, breathwork, anchoring, journaling, intention, visualization, and meditation. Together, these practices support inner listening, emotional regulation, embodied awareness, and congruent action rooted in self-trust. RESULTS: Participants gain a practical understanding of how to access and trust the Christ within (the Voice inside) as a daily, lived resource. The TRANSFORM Method helps dissolve emotional and spiritual limitations, shifts individuals out of performance-driven patterns, and fosters unconditional self-love and self-forgiveness. Her clients experience increased clarity, confidence, and the ability to take ownership of their lives personally and professionally from a place of alignment rather than fear. CONCLUSION: The TRANSFORM Method offers a grounded, compassionate pathway for emotional and spiritual transformation that is experiential, accessible, and sustainable. By activating Christ consciousness (the Voice inside) through embodied practice rather than doctrine, this keynote invites participants to live illuminated, anchored in truth, guided from within, and aligned with who they were created to be. KEYWORDS: Emotional alignment, spiritual leadership, Christ consciousness, self-trust, hypnosis, embodiment, transformation, inner guidance, authenticity, emotional healing Biography: Donna Reiners holds a Bachelor’s degree from Houston Christian University and is a board-certified Quantum Health Coach and board-certified Clinical Hypnotherapist. She is also an ordained minister whose work is Spirit-led rather than religious-led, anchored in relationship with the Creator and with self. As a wife, sister, friend and coach, Donna specializes in guiding women to trust the voice inside. Her work centers on loving oneself completely and unconditionally and forgiving oneself completely and unconditionally, creating the internal safety required for real emotional transformation. She believes the Creator has lived within every person from the beginning of time itself and gently guides others to remember that truth and live from alignment rather than fear. I transform women through Christ Consciousness.

Marie-Anaïs Lopez Marie-Anaïs Lopez TALK TITLE: “ FINDING YOUR VOICE WHEN YOU DOUBT YOURSELF INTRODUCTION: Finding one’s voice is especially difficult in a world saturated with constant noise, rigid expectations, and relentless comparison. For many women, the barrier is not a lack of talent, intelligence, or preparation—it is the quiet, persistent presence of self-doubt shaped by cultural conditioning, past experiences, and internalized expectations. This talk draws on lived experience to offer a powerful reframe: confidence is not a prerequisite for voice; it is a byproduct of using it. Voice does not suddenly appear once certainty is achieved—it is forged through the courageous act of speaking up, even when the voice trembles. AIM: The aim of this talk is to support women in recognizing and using their voice—regardless of background, role, life stage, or self-perception. It centers the idea that every woman already possesses a voice worth hearing, even if it has been muted by doubt, conditioning, or fear of judgment. The objective is to dismantle the deeply rooted belief that confidence must come before action. Instead, the talk reframes voice as a muscle—one that strengthens through intentional choice, repetition, and practice. By speaking up in small, meaningful ways, women begin to build trust in themselves, expand their sense of agency, and redefine confidence as something that grows from action rather than precedes it. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Delivered through personal storytelling and guided reflection, this session centers presence, authenticity, and genuine human connection. Rather than relying on rigid frameworks or prescriptive models, it creates intentional space for participants to see themselves within the narrative and recognize their own lived experiences reflected back to them. Participants are gently invited to explore moments of silence, hesitation, and self-censorship—those subtle yet powerful instances where voice was withheld in the pursuit of safety, approval, or belonging. RESULTS: Participants explore how self-doubt quietly shapes decisions—limiting visibility, voice, and influence even when readiness and expertise are present. The session reveals how internal narratives and fear of judgment drive hesitation, often without conscious awareness. By reframing confidence as an outcome of action rather than a trait, the session offers a practical approach to building self-trust through small acts of expression. Attendees leave better able to recognize moments of choice and consciously choose voice over silence, understanding that confidence grows through practice. CONCLUSION: The talk concludes by reinforcing a foundational truth: voice is not something to be earned through permission, perfection, or external validation—it is something already owned. Every participant is invited to recognize that their voice exists independent of confidence, title, or circumstance, and that reclaiming it is an act of remembering rather than acquisition. The closing reflection weaves together the dual meanings of the French phrases trouver sa voix (finding one’s voice) and trouver sa voie (finding one’s path), illuminating their deep and inseparable connection. As we begin to speak—honestly, imperfectly, and with intention—clarity follows. Direction is not discovered first and expressed later; it emerges through expression. KEYWORDS: Voice, women, leadership, self-doubt, identity Biography: Anaïs Lopez is the CEO of Almaje Languages, a nationally recognised French VCE education business founded in 1999. In 2025, she became the sole owner, successfully navigating the emotional and operational complexities of a multi-decade family business transition. Today, she leads Almaje into its next phase of growth with a clear, future-focused vision that includes expansion into international markets. Anaïs brings nearly 20 years of professional experience across entrepreneurship, Human Resources, and organisational leadership. Her career began in the fitness industry, where she founded and ran a personal training business for six years, working closely with individuals committed to long-term transformation. This early hands-on work shaped her deep understanding of discipline, behaviour change, and the psychology of sustained effort—insights that continue to inform her leadership approach. Alongside her role at Almaje, Anaïs works as a senior Human Resources advisor, supporting organisations through complex people, performance, and change challenges. She is recognised for her candid perspective on imposter syndrome, visibility, and confidence, particularly for women in leadership. Anaïs believes confidence is not a prerequisite for action, but the result of it, and she leads with self-awareness, courage, and a commitment to conscious growth. She is passionate about creating environments where people feel safe to speak, lead, and grow without waiting for certainty or permission. Through her work, Anaïs encourages others to choose action over hesitation and to view confidence as a skill built through practice. CEO of Almaje Languages, specialising in French VCE

Amarilys Galloza Carrero Amarilys Galloza Carrero Talk Title: “Breaking Barriers, Unlocking Potential” INTRODUCTION: Across the globe, neurodevelopmental differences such as autism, ADHD, and anxiety are frequently framed through a deficit-based lens. This narrow perspective overlooks the diverse abilities, adaptive strengths, and meaningful contributions of individuals whose minds work differently. The true societal cost lies not in neurodivergence itself, but in the missed opportunities that result when difference is misunderstood or undervalued. Research in neurodiversity emphasizes that difficulty does not equate to deficiency and that human value extends beyond traditional academic or professional achievement. AIM: The aim of this presentation is to challenge deficit-based narratives surrounding neurodiversity and to highlight how intentional shifts in perspective, combined with inclusive environments, can unlock hidden potential and promote meaningful participation across developmental, cultural, and social contexts. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This presentation integrates: • Clinical practice insights from over 15 years of psychological work with children, adolescents, and adults • Evidence from contemporary neurodiversity research • Lived experience as a parent of an autistic child • Culturally responsive and inclusive assessment and intervention frameworks A reflective, practice-informed approach is used to examine how resilience, self-regulation, and executive functioning can be strengthened within environments that honor identity, language, and culture. RESULTS: Clinical and research evidence shows that neurodevelopmental challenges often coexist with valuable strengths. Inclusive environments foster growth, participation, and meaningful contribution beyond traditional measures of success. CONCLUSION: Moving beyond myths of the “exceptional child,” this keynote affirms a broader truth: all minds carry inherent value. When environments foster belonging rather than comparison, individuals across the neurodiversity spectrum can contribute in powerful and meaningful ways. Recognizing potential in all its forms is not only inclusive it is essential for families, workplaces, and communities to thrive. KEYWORDS: Neurodiversity, Autism, ADHD, Human Potential, Inclusion, Strengths-Based Approach, Executive Functioning, Resilience, Self-Regulation, Creativity, Developmental Growth, Belonging Biography: Amarilys Galloza Carrero, Ph.D. CH-C, CAMS-II. “Breaking Barriers, Unlocking Potential”. For over 15 years, Dr. Amarilys Galloza Carrero has dedicated her career to helping children, adolescents, and adults discover their hidden strengths and create meaningful change. She is a Licensed Clinical Psychologist in Maryland and Virginia (United States), founder of Make It Possible, LLC, and Director of Testing at The Wise Family Wellness Center. A native of Puerto Rico, she holds a Ph.D. in Clinical Psychology from Gallaudet University and is an adjunct professor in the university’s Ph.D. Clinical Psychology program. Dr. Galloza Carrero is a PSYPACT provider, which allows her to practice telehealth across 42 states in the United States. She is also a Certified Clinical Hypnotherapist and Certified Anger Management Specialist Level II. In addition to her clinical and teaching roles, she has contributed to the development of innovative assessment programs and is recognized for advancing culturally responsive evaluation practices. Featured in Top Doctor Magazine and invited to speak nationally and internationally, she is known for her expertise in neurodiversity, Latino psychology, and breaking barriers to accessible care. Her work integrates professional knowledge with her personal journey as a parent of an autistic child, inspiring others to see possibilities where once there were barriers. Licensed Clinical Psychologist, Ph.D., Certified Clinical Hypnotherapist (CH-C), Certified Anger Management Specialist – II (CAMS-II), Founder of Make it Possible, LLC

Amy McDonnell Amy McDonnell Talk Title: “Uncomfortable Courage: The Difference Between Making Noise and MakingProgress INTRODUCTION: This presentation reframes courage as the art of saying the right thing even when the room suddenly gets so quiet you could hear an ego drop. Through storytelling, corporate comedy, and painfully relatable meeting scenarios, this work reveals how courage doesn’t feel heroic, it feels inconvenient, uncomfortable, and absolutely necessary. And yes, sometimes it feels like breaking a sacred rule… because you are. AIM: The aim of this work is to illuminate how Uncomfortable Courage, the slightlysweaty, heart-thumping, “oh no, am really going to say this out loud?” kind, helps women shift from simply making noise to actually making meaningful organizational progress. The goal is to empower leaders to use courage not as a dramatic performance but as a practical, everyday superpower. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Use of real-world leadership moments, observational humor, and dialogue-based case examples to illustrate everyday courage Application of three core courageous behaviors: Clarity Over Comfort, Intentional Disruption Over Accidental Noise, and Voice Over Visibility Training in strategic language and precise timing to speak up effectively without escalating conflict Techniques to build tolerance for discomfort and normalize “raised-eyebrow moments” in professional settings Practical communication tools and reflection prompts for immediate real-world workplace application RESULTS: Leaders who practice Uncomfortable Courage experience sharper decision-making, fewer unproductive discussion spirals, and stronger team alignment. By choosing clarity over comfort, redirecting conversations with intention, and contributing substance over performative visibility, leaders create environments where truth is spoken earlier and problems are addressed before they escalate. Teams become more focused, meetings become more efficient, and collaboration becomes more authentic. An additional outcome is a noticeable cultural shift: coworkers feel relieved and supported when someone finally voices what others were thinking but hesitated to say, often expressing gratitude for the courage shown. As a result, psychological safety increases, trust deepens, and courageous behavior begins to spread organically across teams—driving sustained organizational progress. CONCLUSION: Uncomfortable Courage demonstrates that while noise merely fills space, courage—especially the kind that makes people shift in their chairs—shapes the future of organizations. This work reframes courage as a practical, everyday leadership behavior rather than a dramatic act, showing that meaningful change begins with a single uncomfortable truth spoken at the right moment. When leaders listen to the inner voice that asks, “Should I say something?” and choose to act, they create momentum, clarity, and cultural transformation. Ultimately, this framework affirms that progress belongs to those willing to tolerate discomfort, challenge unspoken rules, and consistently choose courage over comfort. KEYWORDS: Uncomfortable Courage; Conscious Disruption; Clarity; Humorous Influential Communication Clarity Over Comfort; Intentional Disruption; Voice Over Visibility; Everyday Courage; Women in Leadership; Culture Change; Speaking Up; Authentic Leadership; Humor in Leadership; Meeting Dynamics; Organizational Alignment. Biography: Amy McDonnell is a Chief Customer Officer, dynamic executive, former attorney, and unapologetic “conscious disruptor” known for turning corporate confusion into clarity—often with one well-timed question. Leading with curiosity, humor, and courageous candor, she cuts through noise to surface what truly matters, reshaping strategies, shifting mindsets, and making meetings (and decisions) far more effective. A visionary leader with deep expertise in customer experience, revenue growth, and consultative sales, Amy excels at building and motivating high-performing, global teams. She translates complex data into compelling insights for executive and board-level audiences, drives scalable, revenue-generating action, and fosters trusted partnerships that deliver long-term value. Through her leadership and mentorship, she continues to build organizations that are customer-centered, courageous, and designed for sustainable growth. Foundational Builder, Growth Catalyst, GTM Strategist, Customer Relationship Maestro, Angel Investor, Public Speaker

Mary Scott Mary Scott TALK TITLE: THE BRAVE LEADER – CONNECT AND LEAD INTRODUCTION: In an era of rapid change, leadership is no longer defined by authority alone, but by authenticity, emotional intelligence, and the courage to lead from within. Drawing on over 30 years of experience in nursing, psychotherapy, and confidence coaching, Mary Scott introduces a brave leadership model that weaves soulful wisdom with strategic action. This session invites participants to reconnect with their inner authority and redefine leadership as a deeply human, values-driven practice—empowering them to navigate complexity with clarity, courage, and heart. AIM: The aim of this presentation is to empower leaders—particularly those in their second or third life chapter—to replace self-doubt with self-trust, deepen authentic connection, and lead with courage, clarity, and purpose in both personal and professional environments. Participants will be guided to reconnect with their lived experience as a source of wisdom rather than limitation. The session creates space for reflection, renewal, and redefinition of what meaningful leadership looks like at this stage of life. Ultimately, it supports leaders in stepping forward with confidence, integrity, and a renewed sense of contribution. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This presentation uses a reflective and experiential approach, combining real-life case studies, storytelling, evidence-informed psychological insights, and practical confidence-building frameworks. Participants are guided through self-inquiry techniques, connection-based leadership principles, and actionable strategies designed to foster trust, resilience, and authentic influence. The experience encourages deep personal insight while equipping leaders with tools they can immediately apply in their everyday leadership contexts. It also creates a supportive space for shared learning, honest dialogue, and the integration of personal values into effective leadership practice. RESULTS: articipants will gain increased self-trust and confidence in decision-making, along with an enhanced ability to connect authentically with teams and stakeholders. They will also acquire practical tools to lead with emotional intelligence and clarity, enabling more grounded, conscious, and effective leadership in everyday situations. The learning experience supports greater self-awareness and the ability to respond rather than react under pressure. These outcomes support sustainable leadership growth by fostering a renewed sense of purpose and courage in leadership roles—particularly for individuals navigating life transitions or stepping into expanded responsibilities. Participants are encouraged to integrate their values, experience, and vision into their leadership style, strengthening long-term impact. Ultimately, the session empowers leaders to lead with integrity, resilience, and confidence in an evolving professional landscape. CONCLUSION: The Brave Leader – Connect and Lead reframes leadership as an inner journey as much as an external role. By cultivating self-trust, presence, and meaningful connection, leaders can inspire others while remaining aligned with their values and purpose. This session leaves participants empowered to lead boldly, authentically, and with lasting impact—at any stage of life. It offers a powerful invitation to slow down, listen inwardly, and lead from a place of clarity rather than pressure. Participants are supported to integrate insight with action, strengthening both personal fulfilment and professional effectiveness. Ultimately, the experience reinforces leadership as a courageous, conscious practice rooted in humanity and heart. KEYWORDS: Brave Leadership, Confidence, Self-Trust, Authentic Leadership, Emotional Intelligence, Purpose-Driven Leadership, Personal Transformation, Midlife Leadership, Inner Authority, Values-Driven Decision Making, Resilience, Compassionate Influence, Conscious Leadership, Self-Awareness, Meaningful Impact Biography: Mary Scott is a distinguished Confidence Coach, entrepreneur, and published author with over 30 years’ experience guiding individuals through life’s most transformative seasons. With a background spanning 20 years in Nursing and a successful Psychotherapy practice in Melbourne, Australia, her work blends deep insight with practical, soul-aligned action. Mary supports women and men—particularly those 50+—to rediscover confidence, clarify purpose, and step into empowered leadership in life and business. She is the host of The Richness of Our Lives Podcast and leads the Global Rise Up Movement, offering bespoke 1:1 coaching and intimate online communities. An internationally recognised speaker and award recipient, Mary was honoured with the 2025 Ranath Media Lifetime Achievement Award, along with the GIFEW Global Evolutionary Woman Award and the Global Super Mind Award (2024). Talk Title: “The Era of Women Leaders: Why the World Needs Us Now More Than Ever” INTRODUCTION: Across industries, cultures, and generations, leadership models built on control, speed, and authority are no longer meeting the needs of today’s world. As global systems strain under complexity, uncertainty, and rapid change, there is a growing recognition that leadership itself must evolve. This moment marks a profound transition—not simply toward different leaders, but toward a different way of leading. Women around the world are uniquely positioned within this shift, not as replacements for existing systems, but as carriers of a more human-centered, relational, and sustainable leadership orientation. This session explores why the rise of women leaders is not a trend, but a necessary recalibration in how leadership is understood and practiced globally. AIM: The objective of this session is to examine why today’s rapidly shifting global landscape—marked by uncertainty, complexity, and collective fatigue— demands a new model of leadership rooted in hope, trust, compassion, and stability. As traditional dominance-based approaches increasingly fall short, the session highlights why women’s leadership styles are uniquely aligned with the needs of this moment. Participants will explore how leadership is evolving across cultures, generations, and systems, moving away from control and hierarchy toward connection, collaboration, and ethical influence. The session offers insight into the ways women naturally embody these emerging leadership capacities and how they can step into this era with confidence, authenticity, integrity, and grounded presence—without conforming to outdated expectations or leadership archetypes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Keynote presentation with visual storytelling, reflective pauses, global research insights, and facilitated audience reflection. RESULTS: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of the global shifts shaping leadership expectations today, supported by international research and lived leadership experience. The discussion highlights how values such as trust, well-being, meaning, and relational intelligence are increasingly central across cultures and generations. Attendees will be invited to reflect on their own leadership orientation and recognize how leading with humanity, emotional intelligence, and long-term perspective strengthens both people and systems. CONCLUSION: The Era of Women Leaders signals a profound redefinition of leadership at a time when the world is undergoing rapid social, economic, and cultural transformation. Rather than demanding that women lead harder, adapt further, or continually justify their readiness, this moment recognizes a deeper truth: the world itself is ready for the way many women already lead. The prevailing challenges of our time—complexity, uncertainty, polarization, and burnout—have exposed the limitations of dominance-based, extractive leadership models and created an urgent need for approaches grounded in wisdom, care, and relational intelligence. As organizations and institutions confront rising demands for authenticity, psychological safety, and ethical decision-making, leadership rooted in stewardship, presence, empathy, and emotional intelligence is no longer a “soft skill” or optional enhancement—it is a strategic and moral imperative. Women leaders often bring a natural orientation toward listening, integration, and long-term thinking, enabling them to navigate ambiguity while holding space for both people and performance. By leading with relational strength and purpose, women play a vital role in restoring trust, balance, and sustainability within workplaces, communities, and broader systems. Their leadership tends to prioritize meaningful impact over short-term wins, shared ownership over control, and collaboration over hierarchy. KEYWORDS: women’s leadership, global leadership, stewardship, emotional intelligence, trust, compassion, sustainability, human-centered leadership, generational leadership Biography: Anita Pereda, MS is a Holistic Leadership Coach, organizational consultant, and internationally sought-after speaker with over 20 years of experience supporting leaders and organizations through growth, transition, and transformation. Her work is grounded in organizational psychology and conscious leadership, with a focus on human-centered, relational, and sustainable leadership. Anita partners with leaders across cultures and industries as they navigate complexity, uncertainty, and rapid change. Dr. Steve Conway Dr. Steve Conway Talk Title: “The Emotion Inspired Leader” INTRODUCTION: Emotion plays a defining role in leadership, shaping how leaders influence teams, manage challenges, and guide organizational culture. Leaders set the emotional tone of the workplace through their presence, reactions, and relationships. These emotional signals directly affect trust, collaboration, and psychological safety at work. Understanding how emotions operate in leadership helps create healthier, more resilient organizations. Developing emotional awareness is therefore a core leadership responsibility, not an optional skill. AIM: The aim of this presentation is to highlight the central role of emotional intelligence in modern leadership and to demonstrate why emotional awareness, regulation, and relational repair are not optional skills but essential leadership capacities. The session seeks to help leaders understand how their emotional behavior influences engagement, wellbeing, and performance, and to encourage reflective leadership that strengthens trust, resilience, and long-term organizational effectiveness MATERIALS AND METHODS: The session integrates insights from neuroscience, research on psychological safety, and applied leadership practice. It explores three core dimensions of emotionally intelligent leadership: emotional awareness, emotional regulation, and relational repair. Through conceptual explanation, practical examples, and reflective discussion, participants are guided to examine how emotions operate in workplace systems and how leaders can consciously shape healthier, more productive emotional climates within their teams and organizations RESULTS: Leaders who develop emotional competence demonstrate a significantly improved ability to manage conflict, regulate stress, and maintain clarity during periods of pressure and change. Teams led by emotionally intelligent leaders show higher levels of trust, psychological safety, engagement, and collaboration. These environments reduce burnout, improve communication, and strengthen resilience across the organization. Over time, emotionally intelligent leadership contributes to healthier workplace cultures, better decision-making, and more sustainable performance outcomes. The results clearly indicate that emotional competence is not a soft skill, but a critical driver of both human wellbeing and organizational effectiveness. CONCLUSION: Emotional intelligence is not a “soft” skill but a fundamental driver of long-term organizational performance, and leaders must consciously reflect on the emotional impact they have on others to lead effectively in modern workplaces. When leaders understand and manage their own emotions while responding thoughtfully to the emotions of others, they foster trust, psychological safety, and stronger collaboration across teams. This awareness enables more effective communication, reduces conflict, and supports better decision-making under pressure. By modeling empathy, self- regulation, and active listening, leaders create environments where employees feel valued, motivated, and empowered to contribute their best work. Organizations that prioritize emotional intelligence strengthen engagement, innovation, and resilience, ultimately building cultures where both people and performance can thrive together. KEYWORDS: Emotional intelligence, leadership effectiveness, psychological safety, organizational culture, emotional awareness Biography: Steve Conway is an executive and leadership coach, speaker, organizational consultant, and workplace mental health expert. He has spent more than thirty years helping individuals, groups, and organizations thrive, rooted in a long-standing curiosity about how people think, feel, and work together. His approach has been shaped by years of watching how emotion, trust, and presence influence the tone of a workplace and the performance of the people within it. He holds a Doctorate in Psychology and an MBA focused on leadership and teams, along with advanced training in executive coaching and Organization Development. Steve has held senior leadership roles and has lived the same mix of responsibility, uncertainty, and expectation that many leaders face, giving him a grounded, real-world perspective on the challenges people navigate at every level. This helps him understand the work leaders do and the weight they often carry. He engages people in a relatable, human way that encourages honest reflection and meaningful learning, creating space where leaders feel understood and willing to stretch themselves. His speaking style is engaging and inspiring, blending research, insight, and storytelling in a way that moves audiences and stays with them long after the session ends. Steve cares deeply about the kind of workplaces people spend their lives in and works with leaders who want to show up with more awareness, confidence, and humanity. His goal is to help leaders thrive in ways that genuinely improve the lives of the people they lead. Director of Leadership and Psychological Safety | Executive Coach & Speaker | Advancing emotional intelligence, psychological safety, and mentally healthy leadership

Wahida Mohamed Wahida Mohamed Talk Title: “Empowering Voices, Shaping Global Change.” INTRODUCTION: Human stories carry wisdom, values, and life lessons that often remain unheard until it is too late. This talk explores the power of storytelling as a bridge between generations and cultures. By giving voice to lived experiences, storytelling fosters connection, reflection, and personal growth. It creates safe spaces for shared understanding and mutual respect, allowing individuals to feel seen and heard. Through stories, knowledge is preserved, identities are strengthened, and meaningful legacies are passed on. The session highlights how storytelling can deepen empathy, challenge assumptions, and bring diverse perspectives into meaningful dialogue. By listening with curiosity and sharing with authenticity, individuals and communities can build stronger relationships and a greater sense of belonging. Aim: The presentation aims to emphasize the importance of capturing and sharing life stories to preserve wisdom. It seeks to inspire individuals and educators to use storytelling as a tool for motivation, learning, and self-discovery. Encouraging reflective dialogue, it supports deeper emotional engagement and critical thinking. Ultimately, it promotes storytelling as a powerful method for personal empowerment and collective growth. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Grounded in real-life stories and over 30 years of teaching experience, five practical storytelling strategies were developed for educational and community settings. Research-based insights on narrative learning support their effectiveness. These strategies are adaptable across age groups and learning environments, making them accessible and impactful. They encourage active participation, reflection, and meaningful dialogue among participants. RESULTS: Inspires and motivates individuals while transmitting core values. Fosters deeper emotional connection, reflection, and meaning. Encourages openness, mutual understanding, and personal transformation Builds empathy and strengthens relationships across diverse communities. Supports personal growth by validating lived experiences and shared wisdom. Creates lasting impact through meaningful learning and collective insight. CONCLUSION: Every person carries a reservoir of lived wisdom shaped by experiences, challenges, triumphs, and moments of quiet realization. Storytelling is the key that unlocks this wisdom and brings it into the light. When stories are shared, they do more than recount events—they create meaning. They turn individual experiences into shared understanding, allowing personal truths to ripple outward and touch others in profound ways. Storytelling strengthens human connection by reminding us that we are not alone in our struggles, questions, or hopes. A single story can comfort someone in pain, inspire courage in moments of doubt, or offer guidance when the path ahead feels unclear. Through stories, emotions become relatable, lessons become memorable, and empathy grows naturally. They build bridges between people of different backgrounds, generations, and perspectives, fostering a sense of belonging and mutual understanding. Beyond connection, storytelling preserves life lessons and cultural wisdom. Values, traditions, and hard-earned insights are carried forward not as abstract ideas, but as lived experiences filled with context and meaning. This ensures that knowledge is not merely transferred, but felt and remembered. Stories give depth to history and humanity to wisdom, making them accessible and relevant across time. Keywords: Mindset, Personal Development, Self-Confidence, Resilience, Growth, Empowerment Biography: Wahida Mohamed is an author, poet, podcaster, educator, and speaker with over 30 years of experience using storytelling as a powerful tool for learning, connection, and personal growth. Passionate about preserving wisdom through lived experiences, she helps individuals and communities give voice to meaningful stories that inspire, heal, and create lasting impact. Through practical storytelling strategies, Wahida empowers people of all ages to transform everyday experiences into lessons of purpose, connection, and legacy. Mindset & PeAuthor, Poet, Podcaster, Teacher, Public Speaker and Entrepreneur rsonal Development Coach

Aim: Luz’s aim is to empower women who have experienced domestic violence by amplifying their voices and advocating for systemic change. Through her foundation and international platforms, she seeks to promote gender equality, awareness, and survivor-centered solutions. She is committed to aligning creative expression with social impact. Her work focuses on advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those related to women’s rights. Ultimately, her mission is to inspire healing, dignity, and transformation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Luz is a dynamic change-maker who leverages advocacy, public speaking, global partnerships, and nonprofit leadership to advance social transformation on both local and international stages. Her work is rooted in a deep commitment to justice, equity, and human dignity, allowing her to bridge lived experience with systemic change. Through strategic collaboration with international organizations such as the United Nations and UN Women, Luz contributes to policy dialogue, awareness initiatives, and global conversations that address gender-based violence and human rights. These partnerships amplify survivor-centered perspectives and help shape initiatives that are both compassionate and actionable. RESULTS: Her foundation has supported and empowered thousands of domestic violence survivors across multiple countries. Fundación Luz María achieved consultative status with the United Nations ECOSOC, expanding its global reach. Luz was selected as a UN Women Champion for Change from over 5,000 applicants worldwide. Her advocacy has contributed to increased awareness and international dialogue on women’s rights. She has successfully bridged humanitarian work with a renewed, thriving acting career. CONCLUSION: Luz Maria Utrera’s journey exemplifies how adversity can be transformed into purpose and global impact. By uniting creativity, advocacy, and compassion, she has built a legacy that empowers women and influences international change. Her work demonstrates the power of resilience, authenticity, and service-driven leadership, showing how personal experiences can become catalysts for meaningful transformation. Through her initiatives and advocacy, Luz has created spaces where women are encouraged to discover their voice, embrace their strengths, and step into leadership with confidence. Her approach blends creativity with social impact, highlighting how art, storytelling, and community engagement can drive awareness and inspire collective action. Luz continues to inspire individuals worldwide to believe in possibility and purposeful living. Her story stands as a testament that healing and impact can coexist with personal and professional fulfillment, reminding others that challenges can become the foundation for growth, contribution, and lasting change. Keywords: Women’s Empowerment, Domestic Violence Advocacy, Global Leadership, Resilience, Social Impact, UN Sustainable Development Goals Biography: Luz Maria Utrera is an actress, humanitarian, and advocate whose journey blends creativity, resilience, and purpose. After early success in modeling and acting in Argentina, she pursued a law degree in Buenos Aires before relocating to Los Angeles to follow her true calling in acting. There, she trained at the Lee Strasberg Theatre & Film Institute and later served as a judge for the Cinema City International Film Festival. William Davis William Davis Talk Title: “The DNA of Leadership: Building Genuine Relationships ” INTRODUCTION: According to a November 2023 poll, 86% of Americans express profound disappointment in societal leadership, while 78% believe corporate America is facing a crisis of character. This suggests that the traditional, power-based model of management is failing. This session introduces a "people-first" philosophy—the belief that leadership is deceptively simple, yet deeply personal. It moves away from theoretical frameworks and focuses on the genuine emotions and real-world consequences that define the relationship between a leader and their team. AIM: The aim of this work is to explore leadership as a human-centered practice rather than a position of authority, emphasizing the role of authenticity, empathy, trust, and ethical responsibility in achieving sustainable success. Drawing on nearly four decades of real-world leadership experience, the focus is on equipping current and emerging leaders with practical tools and mindsets that foster strong relationships, resilient teams, and positive organizational cultures. Ultimately, the objective is to inspire leaders to lead with heart and vision while driving meaningful and lasting impact. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The insights presented are drawn from nearly four decades of leadership experience across evolving business landscapes, evidenced by a consistent 90% employee retention rate. The methodology focuses on three core pillars of human-centric leadership: Relationship Architecture: Analyzing the "how" and "why" behind building authentic, long-term professional bonds. Applied Empathy: Defining and practicing "Real Empathy" as a functional tool rather than a buzzword. Collaborative Motivation: Shifting the leader’s mindset to view the team as a collective to be inspired rather than a field of competition. RESULTS: By refocusing on the human element, participants will gain the following competencies: Foundational Insight: A transformed view of relationship-building as the primary engine of leadership success. Psychological Safety: An understanding of why sincere empathy strengthens a leader’s position instead of undermining it. Alignment: Direct knowledge of what modern teams actually desire from their leaders to stay engaged and loyal. Emotional Intelligence (EQ): The ability to identify and deploy EQ traits that are critical for navigating modern corporate challenges. CONCLUSION: The evidence is clear: people are looking for more than just a boss; they are looking for a human. The ultimate takeaway is that while business strategies and technologies will continue to shift, the human element remains constant. Treat your team right, and the results will follow. Leadership is—and will always be—about humans. Keywords: Leadership Development; People-First Leadership; Authentic Leadership; Employee Engagement; Ethical Leadership; Trust-Based Leadership; Mentorship; Organizational Culture Biography: William Davis is a seasoned leadership expert, author, mentor, and international speaker with over 38 years of experience leading high- performing teams across corporate America. Known for maintaining a 90%+ employee retention rate throughout his career, William has built a reputation as a people-first leader who believes that true leadership is rooted in trust, empathy, and human connection. His leadership journey began early through his involvement in Future Business Leaders of America, where he developed a deep curiosity about what drives effective leadership. This foundation led to senior leadership roles across multiple industries, where he successfully delivered large-scale projects that created lasting value for organizations while keeping teams engaged and inspired.Today, William is a sought-after keynote speaker and mentor who bridges leadership theory with real-world application. He has written multiple articles for Brainz Magazine and is the author of two books, How to Lead Without Just Managing and Building Genuine Relationships: The Leader’s Guide to Connecting…. Through his speaking, writing, and coaching, William is dedicated to nurturing the next generation of ethical, authentic, and people-centered leaders. Global Keynote Speaker & Author | Human-centric Leadership

Margaret Vuijk-Cieslak Margaret Vuijk-Cieslak Talk Title: “ The Brain on Fire: The Hidden Superpower of a Clear Mind Why It’s Time for Women to Put Themselves First, Rethinking Brain Health, Stress and the Lifestyle That’s Quietly Breaking You Down ” INTRODUCTION: High-performing women around the world are experiencing a silent epidemic of cognitive fatigue, burnout, emotional dysregulation and hormonal imbalance. Often dismissed as “just stress,” these symptoms are rarely recognized for what they truly are: signs of chronic brain-body imbalance caused by prolonged neuroinflammation, HPA axis dysregulation and nervous system overload. The consequences of misdiagnoses, delayed recovery and identity erosion can be long-lasting and life-altering. Despite growing awareness of mental health and brain wellness, few models speak to the unique neurological and hormonal vulnerabilities of women under chronic pressure. When caregiving, careers, and constant performance demands dominate, many women delay self-care until breakdown becomes the body’s only language. AIM: This keynote introduces the ASPIRE ROOT Clarity Process™, a science-based, trauma-aware system for addressing the root causes of cognitive, emotional, and physical exhaustion. Designed for professionals and individuals who have been misdiagnosed or misunderstood, this method helps women recognize hidden brain stress patterns and begin reclaiming their clarity, regulation and capacity to thrive. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Margaret’s work integrates applied neuroscience, brain-body regulation, and trauma-informed coaching to address the root causes of cognitive overload and burnout. Her methods include nervous system recalibration, cognitive energy mapping, sensory and vestibular integration strategies, stress-load reduction, and identity-level reframing following prolonged stress or concussion-related misalignment. Through her ASPIRE ROOT Clarity Process™, she applies structured, evidence-based techniques alongside personalized insight to restore mental clarity, emotional regulation, and sustainable cognitive performance. RESULTS: The ASPIRE ROOT Clarity Process™ has supported clients in reversing cognitive fog, emotional reactivity, chronic exhaustion, and disruptions in focus, clarity, and follow-through, particularly in high-performing women whose symptoms were misunderstood as emotional instability or burnout. This approach was developed after the author’s lived experience surviving multiple concussions and long-term post-concussion symptoms including aphasia, PTSD and depression. These deeply personal experiences, often dismissed or misunderstood, led to the creation of a recovery model that addresses what conventional systems often miss. CONCLUSION: Changing the conversation around brain health, stress and resilience requires a willingness to move beyond surface-level solutions and start addressing the underlying biological and neurological factors. Recovery is not about doing less, it’s about doing differently, in alignment with how the brain and body actually heal. This keynote calls individuals and professionals to: Recognize the hidden symptoms of unresolved brain stress and neuroinflammation Shift from performance-based coping to biology-informed recovery and regulation Reflect critically on personal and systemic patterns that normalize depletion, especially among women and caregivers Begin integrating science-backed, trauma-aware, and sustainable lifestyle strategies that support clarity, energy and long-term brain-body health KEYWORDS: Brain health, neuroinflammation, stress recovery, resilience, cognitive fatigue, nervous system, hormone balance, trauma-informed, lifestyle change, emotional regulation, burnout, women's health, functional medicine, brain-body connection, self-leadership, performance Biography: Margaret Vujik-Cieslak, MSc, is an internationally awarded speaker, Brain Health Strategist, certified neuroscience coach, and Founder of ThinkVuijk. She is the creator of the ASPIRE ROOT Clarity Process™, a proprietary neuroscience-based framework designed to restore cognitive clarity, sustained energy, and neurological resilience after prolonged stress, burnout, and complex brain-body disruption. Drawing on over 15 years in national television journalism and her own lived recovery from multiple concussions, Margaret bridges applied neuroscience, nervous system regulation, and identity restoration. Her work translates complex brain science into practical strategies that support sustainable performance, self-trust, and long-term wellbeing. A sought-after international speaker, she has delivered keynotes for global organizations including Red Bull Racing and works with clients across Europe and North America. She is the author of The Parent’s Handbook on concussion recovery and a co-author of the forthcoming book Unbreakable. Christine Forment Christine Forment Talk Title: “You deserve to know! Stop guessing and start knowing! Start reclaiming your health and sexiness and start loving yourself and your image in the mirror again” INTRODUCTION: Christine Forment has been a diplomat for the last 20 years for the Foreign Services of the European Union to provide aid to development for the population of several tropical “paradise islands”. In the last years, Christine decided to follow her own path and pursue her life mission so she became a nutrition, beauty and wellness and business coach in order to help women over 45+ to age gracefully, younger, healthier and sexier and love themselves and their image in the mirror again. The practice of gathering data about your health is growing globally. In many countries it has been an ancient practice to recommend a daily 5-servings of fruits and vegetables for health and well-being. However, how can you be sure that your habits have the expected impact on your antioxidant and immunity level?How your carotenoid-rich diet and supplements reflect your wellness journey? Unlock personalized insights that inspire choices in your diet, habits, and lifestyle. Bringing awareness about your lifestyle is a key element in enhancing your daily habits for your health and well-being. Aim: Prysm iO helps you understand and improve your wellness by using real research and AI to turn complex health data into one clear, actionable number. This simple score gives you an immediate snapshot of your body’s current state, making wellness easier to understand and manage. MATERIALS AND METHODS: CoPrysm iO uses Spectral Rai Technology, a specific type of light technology, which consists of over 700,000 individual hyperspectral absorption measurements per scan to accurately assess light absorption in the skin. These measurements are converted into your Prysm Score using a predetermined algorithm powered by AI and referencing Raman technology. Using powerful optical techniques, Prysm iO scores skin carotenoid levels in just 15 seconds, offering a simple, non-invasive way to see how your supplement and dietary choices are reflected in your results. RESULTS: Better wellness backed by data proves that small, everyday choices can create powerful, long-term health benefits. Your Prysm score reflects how lifestyle habits influence your antioxidant protection and overall resilience. By making informed decisions in nutrition, movement, and daily routines, you can positively shift your body’s internal balance and clearly see the impact through measurable results. Four key factors that influence your Prysm score include: Eat the rainbow – Filling your plate with colorful fruits and vegetables increases antioxidant and carotenoid intake, strengthening your body’s natural defenses and raising your Prysm score. Skip the smoke – Reducing or eliminating smoking lowers oxidative stress, helping preserve antioxidants and protect cellular health. Focus on fitness – Regular physical activity supports a healthy, balanced BMI, leading to visible improvements in wellness and antioxidant density. Get serious about supplements – Consistent use of high-quality, carotenoid-rich supplements helps support antioxidant levels, especially when dietary intake falls short. Together, these simple yet powerful habits demonstrate how data-backed insights can turn small lifestyle changes into meaningful health wins. CONCLUSION: More than just a way to see your score, the Nu Skin Prysm iO app is your personal wellness guide. It turns your data into clear, meaningful insights that help you make mindful choices. With the right tools and knowledge at your fingertips, see how it responds as you make changes to your diet, supplements, and lifestyle. KEYWORDS: Empowerment, data-driven wellness, antioxidant density, immunity insight, AI-powered health technology, nutrition awareness, lifestyle optimization, skin health, preventive wellness, personalized wellbeing, mindful living, and science-backed self-care. Biography: Christine Forment is a Nutrition, Beauty, Wellness, and Business Coach dedicated to empowering women—especially those 45+—to age gracefully, confidently, and vibrantly. With over 20 years as a diplomat for the European Union’s Foreign Services, her global work in international development shaped a deep understanding of resilience, health, and sustainable well-being. Transitioning from diplomacy into wellness, Christine now helps women reclaim vitality and self-confidence through science-backed, data- driven lifestyle choices. A keynote speaker at international forums and featured in Authority Magazine, she inspires women to age well through mindful nutrition, informed decision-making, and empowered self-care. Stephanie Forbes Stephanie Forbes Talk Title: “ Global Wealth, Local Impact: Women Who Lead from Disruption to Direction. ” INTRODUCTION: Modern women leaders operate in high-pressure, high-stakes environments where expectations are constant. Success is not about finding balance but building systems that work. Sustainable leadership requires more than passion; it demands precision, discipline, and a strategy for preserving clarity amid constant noise. Stephanie Forbes draws on nearly 25 years of experience leading billion-dollar supply chain programs and governance transformations to share insights and practical tools for women navigating complex leadership landscapes. Aim: The aim of this talk is to empower women leaders to navigate high-pressure, male-dominated, and complex organizational environments with strategic clarity and resilience. It seeks to shift the focus from achieving work-life balance to building robust systems and mental models that sustain high performance. Specifically, the talk aims to: provide practical tools for managing overwhelm and decision fatigue; introduce value chain thinking as a framework for understanding and influencing organizational dynamics; equip women to anticipate friction points and make deliberate choices that preserve clarity and authority; foster leadership confidence rooted in capability and strategic thinking rather than external approval; and inspire women to lead unapologetically, sustaining impact, performance, and wellbeing in demanding roles. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Stephanie Forbes presents value chain thinking as a practical leadership framework for navigating complex organizational environments, drawing on nearly 25 years of experience leading global supply chain and governance transformations and insights from her book Global Wealth, Local Impact. She translates strategic concepts into clear, actionable tools that help leaders focus on high-impact decisions and eliminate unnecessary effort. The approach guides participants to anticipate and manage friction from competing priorities and power dynamics while reducing decision fatigue through disciplined prioritization and boundary-setting. By applying value chain logic to leadership challenges, women leaders gain repeatable methods to preserve clarity, strengthen authority, and sustain performance without burnout. RESULTS: Participants develop heightened awareness of the cognitive and emotional patterns that undermine confidence, authority, and strategic clarity in high- pressure leadership environments. Through the practical application of value chain thinking, leaders learn to focus on high-leverage decisions, reduce overwhelm and decision fatigue, and anticipate organizational friction and power dynamics with composure. The session supports reframing internal narratives that drive self-doubt or over-accommodation, strengthening disciplined self-direction, emotional regulation, and stress management. As a result, women leaders enhance executive presence, build trust-based relationships, and expand their influence across complex organizations while sustaining personal wellbeing and long-term performance. CONCLUSION: Leading from the inside out enables women to move from reactive leadership shaped by external expectations to deliberate leadership grounded in clarity, capability, and self-trust. The session underscores that sustainable leadership is built not through balance, but through intentional systems, mental models, and disciplined decision-making that preserve authority and energy over time. By realigning leadership identity with core values, strategic intent, and inner strengths, participants gain the confidence to lead unapologetically in demanding environments. Integrating self-awareness, emotional intelligence, and value chain logic, the talk equips leaders to navigate complexity with composure, inspire trust, and sustain meaningful impact without burnout— demonstrating that high-performing leadership is the result of intentional design of mindset, boundaries, and choices. Keywords: Women leadership, mental health, emotional intelligence, mindfulness, authentic leadership, self-awareness, resilience, mindset, burnout prevention, personal growth. Dr. Denise Y. Wynn Dr. Denise Y. Wynn Talk Title: Permission to Pause: Making Space for Grief in the Workplace INTRODUCTION: Grief is an unavoidable part of the human experience, yet it remains one of the least discussed topics in organizational life. In many workplaces, the expectation of constant productivity leaves little room for employees or leaders to process loss. Whether triggered by personal tragedy, organizational change, or collective trauma, unacknowledged grief can quietly erode engagement, retention, and trust. As organizations face increasing complexity and emotional strain, there is a growing need to recognize grief as a critical, yet often invisible, factor affecting workplace culture and performance. AIM: The aim of this session is to equip leaders, managers, and organizational stakeholders with a deeper understanding of how grief impacts workplace performance, relationships, and overall organizational culture. The session seeks to increase awareness of both visible and invisible forms of grief, including personal loss, professional identity shifts, burnout, and collective or organizational trauma. By increasing grief literacy, the session aims to empower leaders to respond more effectively and compassionately, reduce stigma associated with grief in professional environments, and integrate grief-informed principles MATERIALS AND METHODS: This session will utilize a mixed-method, experiential, and evidence-informed approach. Content will be delivered through a combination of personal narrative, leadership case examples, and current research on grief, emotional labor, and psychological safety in organizational settings. Interactive elements such as guided reflection, facilitated group discussion, and practical scenario-based learning will be incorporated to enhance participant engagement and real-world application. Participants will be introduced to grief-informed leadership frameworks and practical tools designed to help them recognize grief responses, communicate with empathy, and implement supportive workplace practices. RESULTS: Studies indicate that organizations leveraging predictive analytics and system-level decision-making significantly outperform peers in agility, resilience, and profitability. However, many leaders continue to use data primarily for reporting rather than anticipation. This keynote reframes data as a design instrument—a tool for forecasting friction, identifying repeating patterns, and engineering outcomes before crises emerge. Participants will explore how elite leaders move from reactive management to intentional future design by: Using predictive leadership to shift from hindsight to foresight Applying pattern recognition to uncover hidden inefficiencies and growth constraints Adopting big system thinking to understand how decisions ripple across organizations and ecosystems The discussion highlights how women leaders who master these capabilities gain disproportionate influence in environments defined by uncertainty and rapid change. CONCLUSION: When organizations give permission to pause, they send a clear and powerful message that people are valued for more than their productivity. This intentional shift allows space for reflection, humanity, and emotional acknowledgment—especially during times of grief, loss, or significant transition. Grief- informed leadership recognizes that moments of loss, when approached with empathy and presence, can become opportunities for deeper connection, healing, and collective renewal rather than disruption. KEYWORDS: Grief in the workplace, compassionate leadership, emotional resilience, empathy, organizational culture, psychological safety, grief-informed leadership Biography: Dr. Denise Y. Wynn is the Founder and Principal of Wynn Essentials LLC, where she helps organizations and leaders navigate change with empathy, strategy, and purpose. With over 25 years of experience in research administration and higher education leadership, she offers a unique combination of operational expertise and human-centered insight work. Dr. Wynn is the author of Permission to Pause: Making Space for Grief in the Workplace, which explores how compassionate leadership and emotional awareness can transform organizational culture. Her research and training focus on grief-informed leadership, psychological safety, and the link between workplace wellness and performance. A sought-after speaker and educator, Dr. Wynn delivers keynotes, workshops, and executive training programs that inspire professionals to lead with humanity, resilience, and authenticity. She holds a Doctor of Business Administration (DBA), an MBA, and dual bachelor’s degrees in Accounting and Computer Information Systems. Bruce Wren Bruce Wren Talk Title: “The Bruce³ Blueprint: Building Leadership Principles into Transformational Impact” INTRODUCTION / BACKGROUND: In today’s rapidly evolving business landscape, leadership must be more than positional—it must be principled and transformational. The Bruce Blueprint® is based upon the Bruce³ System (Branding, Resilience, Understanding, Communications) and the E³ Model (Executing, Engagement, Empowerment) were designed to equip leaders with the clarity, confidence, and capacity to lead with purpose and deliver measurable impact. With over two decades of experience in executive coaching and leadership development, I am proud to share that these frameworks will be further explored in my upcoming book on principled leadership, The Bruce Blueprint. Tameka L Payton Tameka L Payton Talk Title: “The Only or the Other: Navigating Psychometrics, Leadership, and Presence as a Woman of Color” INTRODUCTION: Psychometrics is a scientific discipline focused on the design, analysis, and validation of assessments measuring human abilities, traits, and psychological constructs. It requires advanced expertise in statistics, psychology, and measurement theory to ensure reliability, validity, fairness, and scientific rigor across educational, licensure, employment, and clinical contexts. Despite its technical sophistication, the field remains predominantly White and male, with Black women among the most underrepresented professionals. These demographic imbalances shape professional norms, expectations, and experiences related to identity, belonging, and leadership. AIM: To examine the lived experience of navigating the highly technical and demographically imbalanced field of psychometrics as a Black woman, and to identify strategies for transforming professional marginalization into leadership, influence, and authentic self-authorship. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This presentation employs an autoethnographic narrative methodology, drawing on the presenter’s lived experiences across academic, governmental, and professional psychometric contexts. Through reflective storytelling and critical self-analysis, the work situates personal experience within broader structural, cultural, and institutional dynamics, allowing individual moments to illuminate systemic patterns. Reflective case analysis is used to examine instances of professional othering, erasure, and microaggressions, including moments such as being collectively referred to as “the two Tamekas.” These incidents are analyzed not as isolated interpersonal missteps, but as culturally embedded practices that reveal how identity, visibility, and professional credibility are negotiated, constrained, and contested within predominantly White, male-dominated environments. RESULTS: The analysis demonstrates that professional isolation and recurring microaggressions play a substantial role in shaping identity formation, self-perception, and career navigation within high-status, exclusionary professional environments. These experiences influence not only how individuals are perceived by others, but also how they learn to interpret signals of belonging, credibility, and legitimacy over time. Despite these structural challenges, the findings illuminate a set of deliberate strategies that enabled persistence, resilience, and upward mobility. Central among these was the reframing of marginalization as data—treating moments of exclusion not as personal deficiencies, but as informative indicators of organizational norms, power dynamics, and unspoken rules. This cognitive shift allowed for strategic decision-making rather than internalized self-doubt. CONCLUSION: The presentation illustrates how professional “only-ness”—being the only woman, the only person of color, or the only one with a different perspective—can shift from a source of isolation into a powerful foundation for influence and leadership. Rather than requiring assimilation or self-erasure, it highlights how intentional strategy, technical excellence, and conscious self-authorship enable individuals to define their own leadership narrative. By strengthening credibility, clarifying values, and making impact visible, “only-ness” becomes a strategic advantage rather than a limitation. Grounded in research and tested through lived experience, these insights offer practical pathways for women and leaders of color to navigate and reshape inequitable professional systems from within. The approach emphasizes maintaining authenticity while exercising authority—demonstrating that influence does not require conformity. Instead, sustainable leadership emerges when individuals claim their voice, lead with confidence, and actively participate in transforming organizational cultures to be more equitable, inclusive, and future-ready. KEYWORDS: Psychometrics, Diversity in STEM, Women of Color, Leadership, Measurement Science, Only-ness, Professional Identity Biography: Tameka L. Payton, Ph.D. is a distinguished psychometrician, equity-driven innovator, and Founder & CEO of Psychometric Solutions. With an interdisciplinary background spanning psychometrics, educational leadership, and mental health counseling, she brings a deeply human- centered approach to measurement science. Dr. Payton holds a Ph.D. in Psychometrics, dual master’s degrees in Human Resource Development and Mental Health Counseling, and is a Licensed Graduate Professional Counselor. She partners with state agencies, certification boards, and national organizations to design and validate assessments that are rigorous, defensible, and equitable. Her work advances fairness in high- stakes testing, workforce credentialing, and professional certification. As one of the few women of color in psychometrics, Dr. Payton is a powerful advocate for diversity in STEM and leadership development for women of color. Through her scholarship and consulting, she challenges traditional norms and redefines ethical, inclusive measurement across education, workforce, and mental health systems. Founder, CEO, and Chief Visionary@ Psychometric Solutions | PhD in Psychometrics

Dr. Magbor E. Atem Dr. Magbor E. Atem Talk Title: Value Beyond Numbers™: Leading the Future Before It Arrives—How Women Use Systems, Strategy, and Foresight to Shape What’s Next INTRODUCTION: In an increasingly complex and volatile global environment, organizations are generating more data than ever before—yet many leaders remain reactive, relying on reports that explain the past rather than systems that shape the future. While data abundance has grown, true strategic foresight remains scarce. Research shows that although women make up approximately 43% of the global workforce, they hold only about 30% of senior leadership roles, often positioned as operators or analysts rather than architects of decision-making systems. This keynote challenges that paradigm by reframing leadership through the Value Beyond Numbers™ framework—positioning women leaders not as participants within existing systems, but as designers of future-ready strategies powered by predictive leadership, pattern recognition, and big-system thinking. AIM: The objective of this keynote is to equip women leaders with a future-focused leadership model that transcends traditional operational efficiency and retrospective analytics. Specifically, this session aims to: Introduce predictive leadership as a critical competency for navigating uncertainty Demonstrate how pattern recognition enables leaders to anticipate risk, opportunity, and disruption Position big system thinking as a foundation for sustainable authority, scalability, and global impact Participants will gain clarity on how to convert data into strategic insight and insight into influence—well before disruption occurs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This keynote will be delivered through a structured, narrative-driven presentation supported by visual frameworks and applied leadership models. The approach integrates: Systems thinking and predictive strategy concepts Industry insights drawn from operational transformation, technology, and leadership research Interactive reflection prompts designed to engage executive level thinking and strategic self-assessment The session emphasizes synthesis, foresight, and real-world applicability rather than technical complexity. RESULTS: Studies show that organizations using predictive analytics and system-level decision-making outperform peers in agility, resilience, and profitability. Yet many leaders still rely on data for reporting rather than anticipation. This keynote reframes data as a design tool—used to forecast friction, recognize patterns, and shape outcomes before disruption occurs. Participants explore how forward-thinking leaders shift from reactive management to future-focused leadership by applying predictive insight, pattern recognition, and big-system thinking. The session highlights how women leaders who master these capabilities gain outsized influence in fast-changing, high-uncertainty environments. CONCLUSION: As a result of this session, participants are expected to develop increased awareness of how grief manifests in professional settings and how it influences engagement, trust, decision-making, and team dynamics. Participants will be better equipped to identify signs of grief and emotional strain in themselves and others, respond with empathy and appropriate boundaries, and apply grief-informed strategies to support individuals and teams.
