Arsella Burton Arsella Burton TALK TITLE: DISPARITIES IN GLOBAL WOMEN CEO REPRESENTATION AND COMPENSATION INTRODUCTION: Although women represent nearly half of the global workforce, they remain significantly underrepresented in CEO and executive leadership roles worldwide. This disparity reflects persistent structural, cultural, and economic barriers that limit women’s advancement to the highest levels of corporate decision-making. Given the influence of executive leadership on organizational performance and societal outcomes, addressing gender gaps in CEO representation and compensation is both an equity and economic imperative. This study examines global trends, regional variations, and systemic challenges affecting women’s access to top executive roles and equitable compensation AIM: The aim of this study is to examine global gender disparities in CEO representation and executive compensation across diverse regions and economic contexts. It analyzes the structural, organizational, and cultural barriers that restrict women’s access to senior executive and CEO-level positions, while evaluating leadership pathways and compensation frameworks where inequities persist. By synthesizing global data and comparative insights, this research outlines practical, evidence-based strategies to promote inclusive leadership development and equitable pathways for women aspiring to top corporate roles. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study adopts a qualitative research design grounded in secondary data analysis drawn from global labor force statistics, executive compensation reports, and peer-reviewed academic literature. A comparative analytical framework is applied across key regions, including North America, Europe, and Asia, to identify trends, regional variations, and patterns in gender-based disparities in CEO representation and compensation. In addition, the study incorporates selected case studies from countries demonstrating higher levels of female CEO representation to examine institutional, cultural, and policy- related enabling factors. -The findings are synthesized and presented through a structured PowerPoint presentation and an engaging TED Talk–style format to ensure clarity, accessibility, and broad audience impact RESULTS: Findings reveal that while countries like Thailand and China have made notable progress, the global average remains low. Women underrepresented in CEO roles and face significant compensation gaps. The data suggests that internal promotion pathways, mentorship access, and cultural perceptions of leadership play critical roles in shaping these outcomes. Moreover, compensation disparities driven by unequal access to bonuses and long-term incentives. CONCLUSION: The findings of this study highlight that, despite modest and uneven progress across certain regions, women continue to be markedly underrepresented in CEO roles worldwide and face persistent disparities in executive compensation. These inequities are not the result of a lack of capability or ambition, but rather the consequence of deeply embedded structural and systemic barriers that limit women’s access to top leadership opportunities. Key obstacles include restricted access to mentorship and sponsorship networks, opaque promotion and succession processes, and enduring cultural norms and biases that influence perceptions of leadership and authority. Together, these factors create compounding disadvantages that hinder women’s progression into the highest levels of organizational leadership and contribute to ongoing pay inequities at the executive level. To meaningfully close these gaps, organizations must move beyond symbolic commitments and adopt intentional, data-driven strategies. Strengthening CEO succession pipelines through targeted leadership development, sponsorship programs, and equitable talent identification practices is critical. KEYWORDS: Women CEOs, Gender Disparity, Executive Leadership, Compensation Equity, Global Workforce, Inclusive Leadership. Most recently, she supported the Defense Health Administration in expanding managed long-term care benefits for TRICARE For Life beneficiaries, collaborating with federal agencies and policymakers to enhance healthcare access and equity. Deborah S. Greenhut Deborah S. Greenhut TALK TITLE: TOO MUCH OF A GOOD THING: RECONSIDERING WHAT WE ASK OF FAMILY CAREGIVERS INTRODUCTION: Caregiving is often cited as an indication of civilization. Many conditions require assistance from other people for human survival. At this time in history, the fact that people are living longer, and medicine and technology are helping them to do so has spotlighted a burgeoning need for more caregivers than ever to maintain people’s quality of life. The average age of a first-time caregiver, typically a woman, is 42 years old. If her loved one or caree is chronically ill, but surviving into their 70s, the three decades of care, if they have been mostly solo, will have also taken their toll on the caregiver. We have come to identify a “caregiver syndrome,” which some call “caregiver burden”—its cause is chronic stress. AIM: Caregiving is overwhelming due to unrealistic expectations, limited support, and emotional, physical, and financial strain. Families and institutions often rely on unpaid caregivers without adequate resources or relief. True empowerment comes through education, shared responsibility, and access to support systems. A “sharegiving” approach helps protect caregivers’ well-being while ensuring sustainable care. MATERIALS AND METHODS: For this talk, I will work from prepared slides and engage the thought process of the audience with a set of questions about preparedness so that the participants can begin to tackle this issue for their own families or themselves. RESULTS: When people leave the meeting, they will be more fully aware of the obstacles to empowerment for women caregivers and ideas for how to remove them. Family Caregivers have no department of human resources to determine their fitness for the job—they simply must plunge in and do it because it usually begins as an emergency. Families need to make this aspect a part of their emergency preparedness so that people understand their roles and expectations and have at least general knowledge of the assignments they will take on before the pressure comes. Empowerment will come from knowledge, not the ignorance that so many people bear regarding events that are now common for around 20 percent of the global population between caregivers and those who need them. CONCLUSION: Expecting people to work around the clock without compensation or relief is simply not a realistic way to maintain some people’s quality of life at the expense of others. If we do not empower caregivers to get their needs met, many will not be able to complete their assignments, and this will cause an additional large number of people to sustain illness and possibly early death to service a problem that causes many people to look away. Beyond thinking of revising caregiving to provide more “help,” to caregivers, we need to think of how to put ourselves into the process, offering intentional acts of kindness not to make only ourselves feel good about our goodness, but to serve the people who have shown the humanity to serve others. KEYWORDS: Empowerment, Caregiver burden, Stress, Well-being, Wellness, Mindset, Co-Dependence vs. Empowerment, Decision Making, Management, Planning Leading, Controlling, Serving, Sacrifice, Caregiver-Recipient Relationships, Community Support, Delegation, Support Network, Premature mortality, Random Acts of Kindness, Caregiver, Caree, Medical Technology, Service. Biography: International Speaker, Author, Educator and three-time family caregiver, Deborah S. Greenhut, PhD is passionate about sharing her experiences to help other family caregivers set boundaries for effective family caregiving. Deborah's recently published book, "The Rational Caregiver," an Amazon Best Seller and Top New Release, shares her framework for approaching caregiving with rational awareness, acceptance, and responsibility to survive caregiving. During her consulting and training career, she developed and delivered communication, problem-solving, and TQM facilitations skills to corporations, government services, and academic organizations throughout North America and in Western Europe in addition to fostering literacy improvement in K-12 schools. Dr. Greenhut graduated Phi Beta Kappa with a B.A. from Middlebury College and holds a PhD from Rutgers University. A prize-winning poet, she authored an award-winning novel, The Hoarder’s Wife, published by Woodhall Press in 2022, a personal look at the devastating consequences of untreated mental health issues within a family. Deborah’s first book was a study of British poetry about women and silence in the era of Queen Elizabeth. Dr. Greenhut shares her love of writing with Senior Citizens by teaching Memoir Writing at the Rutgers University Osher Online Learning Institute. Deborah S. Greenhut is listed in Who’s Who in America 2024-2025. President, Princeton Research Forum; President, Creative Room for Learning; published SPEAKer Amazon Best-Selling Author The Rational Caregiver

Candace Bazemore Candace Bazemore TALK TITLE: UNSTOPPABLE BY DESIGN: CREATING WEALTH THROUGH LEADERSHIP, EXPERTISE & AI-POWERED SYSTEMS INTRODUCTION: In today’s rapidly evolving global economy, women leaders are being called not only to lead teams and initiatives, but to intentionally design, own, and build systems that generate long-term and generational value. As technology, automation, and AI reshape how work is done, leadership increasingly requires the ability to create scalable structures that extend impact beyond individual effort.Traditional leadership models often prioritize execution over ownership, positioning women as high-performing contributors while limiting their economic agency. This session reframes wealth creation as a leadership responsibility rather than a side pursuit, encouraging women to align purpose, expertise, and strategic ownership to sustain impact without overextension. AIM: This workshop aims to empower women leaders to intentionally recognize and leverage their leadership experience, professional expertise, and institutional influence as valuable, transferable assets. Rather than relying solely on time-bound effort, participants are guided to reimagine their skills and authority as foundations for scalable systems that amplify impact and extend reach.Through a practical and future-focused lens, the session supports women in designing structures that align purpose with sustainability and economic agency. By shifting from execution to intentional system-building, participants are equipped to create long-term value, resilience, and wealth while maintaining integrity and mission-driven leadership. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Grounded in real-world experience across digital transformation, higher education leadership, and entrepreneurship, this workshop combines practical frameworks with guided strategic reflection. The approach encourages participants to critically examine their current leadership roles, decision-making patterns, and value creation pathways, while offering future-focused insights that bridge strategy and execution. Participants explore how AI-powered systems, automation, and strategic infrastructure can be intentionally applied to reduce over-reliance on manual effort and linear work models. Through applied examples and structured discussion, the session illustrates pathways to greater efficiency, ownership, and scalability—enabling women leaders to design systems that support both professional impact and long-term wealth creation. RESULTS: participants gain deeper clarity on how to reposition their knowledge, experience, and leadership capabilities as strategic, wealth-building assets rather than solely sources of earned income. This workshop equips participants with the clarity and confidence to lead as owners, architects, and decision-makers in the age of intelligent systems. By embracing ownership, strategic design, and AI-enabled leverage, women are positioned to lead with authority and intention—shaping futures that reflect their values, expand opportunity, and create lasting personal and professional legacy. Alina Voronova Alina Voronova Talk Title: “ Emotions Are Data, Not Drama Learn to decode signals and lead with precision ” INTRODUCTION: TIn contexts of rapid change and sustained pressure, leadership increasingly intersects with emotional regulation and mental wellbeing. Many leaders operate in high-visibility roles where emotional signals—immediate, subtle, and relational—strongly influence decision-making. Highly sensitive and emotionally attuned leaders often experience these signals as overload rather than information. This is particularly pronounced for women leaders, whose emotional awareness is frequently misinterpreted as vulnerability. As a result, emotions are often suppressed or ignored instead of being understood and used strategically. AIM: The aim of this presentation is to reframe empathy as a practical leadership skill that enhances clarity, authority, and effective decision-making under pressure. It differentiates empathy from emotional fusion, demonstrates how emotions can be understood and used as actionable data, supports leaders in applying emotional sensitivity without becoming overwhelmed, and strengthens leadership presence through self-acceptance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The presentation follows a TED-style experiential format that combines narrative insight, conceptual framing, and brief reflective exercises. The approach is practitioner-based and non-clinical, drawing on over two decades of professional experience rather than original empirical research. Methods include a short guided self-observation exercise, a clear conceptual model distinguishing empathy from emotional fusion, applied leadership examples, and a brief integration exercise. All interactive elements are designed to be minimal, psychologically safe, and immediately applicable in leadership contexts. RESULTS: Across leadership roles, industries, and cultural contexts, leaders consistently demonstrate strong professional competence while experiencing difficulty in interpreting emotional signals. Emotions are frequently perceived as internal pressure or self-doubt rather than understood as neutral information emerging from relational and systemic environments. This misinterpretation contributes to cognitive overload and reactive leadership behaviors, particularly under sustained stress and high visibility. When leaders develop the ability to pause and decode emotional input rather than absorb or suppress it, significant shifts occur. Decision-making becomes clearer as internal noise decreases, communication becomes more direct, and leadership presence stabilizes. The distinction between empathy and emotional fusion proves critical: calibrated empathy preserves sensitivity while maintaining boundaries. For women leaders, this reframing reduces emotional labor and avoidance of visibility, while strengthening self-trust and authority. CONCLUSION: Emotional sensitivity has long been framed as incompatible with effective leadership, reinforcing the belief that emotions must be minimized or controlled to maintain authority. This perspective overlooks the role emotions play as informational signals within complex systems. Uninterpreted emotions increase instability, while accurately decoded emotions support clarity, regulation, and intentional decision-making. Empathy, when structured and regulated, functions as a leadership capability rather than a personal trait. Leaders do not need to feel less to lead better; they need to interpret emotional data accurately and respond with intention. Treating emotions as data rather than drama enables leadership that is calmer, more decisive, and more sustainable, particularly in high-pressure and high-visibility environments. KEYWORDS: Empathetic leadership; emotional intelligence; women in leadership; emotional decision-making; mental health in leadership; empathy vs emotional fusion; emotional climate; sustainable leadership. Biography: Alīna Voronova is a Life Balance Coach specializing in leadership under pressure, emotional decision-making, and sustainable renewal. With over 20 years of experience in personal transformation, she supports entrepreneurs and senior leaders in interpreting emotional signals as actionable data rather than disruption. Trained extensively in advanced hypnotherapy in France, Alīna integrates systemic thinking, subconscious processes, and nervous system regulation to help leaders strengthen clarity, self-trust, and presence in high-stakes environments. Her work is particularly impactful for women leaders, reframing emotional sensitivity as a leadership asset and enabling sustainable authority without emotional overload or burnout. She helps leaders distinguish empathy from emotional fusion, reducing emotional overload while strengthening decisiveness and leadership stability. Her methodology emphasizes internal regulation as the foundation of effective leadership, enabling clarity, confidence, and sustainable presence across diverse organizational and cultural contexts. Alīna works internationally with leaders navigating rapid growth, increased visibility, and complex decision-making. Her work supports sustainable performance by aligning inner regulation with external authority and strategic action. Coach for entrepreneurs in times of change and stress | Systemic thinking, emotional climate, sustainable renewal

Russell W Strand Russell W Strand Talk Title: Human-Centric Engagement: The Art and Science of Authentic Connection to Reduce Violence Against Women INTRODUCTION: Violence against women remains a critical global issue, persisting across homes, workplaces, schools, and communities despite existing prevention and response systems. In many cases, wellintentioned professional interventions unintentionally cause further harm due to a lack of authentic human connection. Strengthening meaningful, empathetic engagement is essential for effective prevention, response, and healing. AIM: The aim of this workshop is to explore the role of authentic human connection in reducing violence against women and other harmful behaviors, while enhancing the effectiveness of leaders, helping professionals, first responders, and organizations in prevention and victim-centered response. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The session draws on decades of professional experience, evidence-based research, case studies, and real-world examples from violence prevention, victim advocacy, and human-centered engagement practices. This presentation uses a mixed-method approach, combining research insights with experiential learning, reflective discussion, and practical strategies. Participants are guided through key components of authentic connection—empathy, compassion, vulnerability, dignity, and hope— and how to apply them in professional and personal contexts. RESULTS: Through this session, participants gain a deeper and more comprehensive understanding of how authentic human connection strengthens prevention efforts, reduces secondary harm, and supports meaningful healing for victims and survivors of violence and trauma. Participants develop increased awareness of the critical role empathy, compassion, and dignity play in shaping safer systems and more responsive communities. They explore how human-centered engagement improves outcomes across prevention, intervention, and recovery, and how relational approaches can interrupt cycles of harm before they escalate. The session enhances participants’ ability to build trust with individuals and communities, respond effectively and sensitively to trauma, and navigate complex emotional and relational dynamics with confidence and care. Participants strengthen their capacity to create environments where people feel seen, heard, believed, and supported. CONCLUSION: Authentic human connection is a foundational force in reducing violence against women and addressing all forms of human-caused harm. When individuals, professionals, and communities engage with one another through empathy, dignity, and genuine care, they create the conditions necessary for safety, trust, and lasting change. Most importantly, authentic connection supports meaningful healing. It empowers survivors to reclaim their voice, rebuild trust, and restore their sense of agency. It enables communities to respond with courage and responsibility. When we lead with humanity, we build safer communities, stronger systems of care, and a future rooted in respect, equity, and shared responsibility. KEYWORDS: Human-Centered Engagement, Violence Against Women, Authentic Connection, Empathy, Prevention, Trauma-Informed Practice, Leadership, Victim Advocacy Biography: Russell W. Strand is a retired Senior Federal Special Agent and a nationally and internationally recognized expert in the response to and prevention of crimes against persons. His extensive career includes leadership roles as a Sexual Harassment & Assault Response & Prevention (SHARP) Program Manager, Victim Advocate, and Violence Prevention Program Manager. With more than 50 years of specialized experience, Russ has worked extensively with offenders, victims, and survivors of crime, addressing harmful behaviors such as child abuse, interpersonal violence, sexual harassment and assault, human trafficking, and death investigations. He is widely respected for his ability to translate complex investigative and behavioral insights into effective prevention, education, and response strategies. Russ has received visionary awards from both End Violence Against Women International and St. Luke’s Health System in recognition of his impact and leadership in the field. Throughout his career, he has designed and delivered prevention, training, and criminal justice education programs through plenaries and workshops, personally reaching and educating well over 800,000 professionals worldwide Senior Special Agent (Retired), Program Manager, Consultant, Educator, and Keynote Speaker

Ann-Marie Emmanuel Ann-Marie Emmanuel Talk Title: “Redefining Success: From Superwoman to Self-Love” INTRODUCTION: Many people reach a stage in life where external success appears complete, yet an inner voice quietly asks, “Is this all?” This presentation explores that inner conflict and the emotional and spiritual journey that begins when the life we have built no longer feels aligned with who we truly are. It examines how the pursuit of achievement, control, and certainty can distance us from our authentic selves and how self-love becomes the path back to inner truth. The session invites participants to reflect on the expectations, roles, and narratives that may have shaped their choices, often without conscious awareness. Through guided reflection and practical insights, it highlights how reconnecting with personal values, emotions, and purpose can restore clarity and meaning. By embracing self-compassion, authenticity, and intentional change, individuals learn to move from living by external measures of success to living with inner alignment and fulfillment. This journey opens the door to renewed purpose, deeper connection, and a more meaningful way of living. AIM: The aim of this session is to redefine success from an internal perspective and to guide individuals toward reconnecting with their authentic selves through unconditional self-love, inner awareness, and personal realignment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The session uses reflective storytelling, guided self-inquiry, emotional awareness exercises, and mindset reframing to help participants: Identify misalignment between external success and internal fulfillment Recognize emotional burnout and inner disconnection Reframe life challenges as transformational turning points Cultivate self-love as a daily, lived practice RESULTS: As a result of this session, participants experience a profound shift in perspective regarding success, identity, and personal fulfillment. They gain clarity about the emotional and psychological costs of pursuing externally defined success and develop a renewed understanding of what it means to live in alignment with their authentic values. Attendees report increased self-awareness, emotional resilience, and self-compassion, along with a stronger ability to recognize misalignment and make conscious, empowered life choices. Many begin to reframe life disruptions, burnout, and “rock bottom” experiences not as failures, but as necessary turning points for growth, healing, and reinvention. The overall outcome is a deeper sense of inner peace, purpose, and wholeness, supported by a practical and sustainable commitment to self-love as the foundation of true success. CONCLUSION: True success is not found in external achievements or changing circumstances, but in returning to oneself. When self-love becomes the foundation of life, peace, purpose, and fulfillment follow naturally. The journey home to one’s own heart becomes the most meaningful and transformative journey of all. This perspective invites individuals to redefine success through alignment, authenticity, and inner well-being rather than external validation. By cultivating self-acceptance and compassion, people can release pressure, quiet self-doubt, and reconnect with what truly matters. As this inner foundation strengthens, decisions become clearer, relationships deepen, and life begins to reflect a greater sense of harmony and intention. In this way, personal fulfillment grows from within and radiates outward into every area of life. Adrienne Tilli Adrienne Tilli Talk Title: “Travel as Therapy – The Connection Between Health & Tourism.” INTRODUCTION: In today’s fast-paced and high-stress global environment, traditional approaches to healthcare often focus on symptom management rather than prevention and holistic well-being. Concurrently, the tourism industry is evolving beyond leisure toward meaningful, restorative experiences. The integration of healthcare, wellness innovation, and travel has given rise to health tourism, positioning travel as a therapeutic modality that supports physical vitality, emotional balance, and mental clarity. This emerging paradigm recognizes the profound impact that environment,. AIM: This presentation aims to explore travel as therapy by examining how healthcare-integrated tourism models can support preventive health, early intervention, and sustainable well-being. It seeks to demonstrate how personalized medical diagnostics combined with experiential travel can empower individuals to take an active role in their health while fostering self-awareness, resilience, and lifestyle transformation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The approach is based on interdisciplinary practice combining health tourism, holistic medicine, and personalized healthcare services. Insights are drawn from the global implementation of the SBT MED Biomedical Clinic model, including the use of innovative diagnostic technologies such as ZYTO Technology and iMirror, alongside case experiences from international healthcare-tourism settings.Case experiences from international healthcare-tourism programs were analyzed to evaluate patient engagement, health awareness, and preventive outcomes. The model emphasizes individualized assessment, non- invasive diagnostics, lifestyle guidance, and continuous monitoring within supportive travel environments that promote relaxation, reflection, and healing. RESULTS: Findings indicate that participants engaging in healthcare-supported travel experiences demonstrate increased awareness of their physical and emotional health, improved stress regulation, and enhanced motivation for lifestyle change. Early detection of imbalances through advanced diagnostic tools enabled timely preventive interventions, reducing long-term health risks. Patients reported improved well-being, heightened self-responsibility for health decisions, and greater satisfaction with personalized care models. The SBT MED approach has successfully reached tens of thousands of individuals across international markets, demonstrating scalability, adaptability, and positive health engagement outcomes. CONCLUSION: Travel, when intentionally designed and supported by medical innovation, can function as a powerful therapeutic and preventive tool. Integrating healthcare with tourism creates an opportunity for deeper healing, proactive wellness management, and personal transformation. This model redefines health tourism as a sustainable pathway to long-term well-being, positioning travel not merely as an escape, but as an essential component of conscious, preventive healthcare. By combining medical expertise with restorative environments, individuals can address physical, emotional, and mental well-being in a holistic way. Preventive screenings, recovery programs, wellness retreats, and lifestyle coaching can be seamlessly integrated into travel experiences, encouraging people to take a proactive role in their health. This approach also promotes global collaboration, expands access to specialized care, and supports healthier lifestyle habits that continue long after the journey ends. When travel is aligned with well-being, it becomes a catalyst for lasting health, renewed energy, and sustainable personal growth. KEYWORDS: Health Tourism, Travel as Therapy, Preventive Healthcare, Holistic Wellness, Personalized Medicine, Medical Innovation, Selfness, Sustainable Well-being Biography: Adrienne Tilli is an accomplished entrepreneur, economist, and global leader in the field of holistic health tourism and preventive healthcare innovation. She serves as the Owner and Managing Director of the SBT MED Biomedical Clinic International Network, a pioneering global healthcare model integrating advanced diagnostics with personalized wellness solutions. She is also the President of Skål International Hungary – Budapest, a prestigious global tourism organization promoting ethical leadership and sustainable tourism. Adrienne holds academic qualifications in Business Administration, EU-focused SME Development, Home Staging, and Clinical Aromatherapy, bringing a unique multidisciplinary perspective to her work. She began her professional journey in tourism at the age of 17, later founding her own travel company before transitioning into real estate and healthcare tourism, where she identified the transformative potential of combining travel with preventive medicine. In collaboration with Prof. Dr. Tamás Sebestény, Adrienne co-founded the SBT MED Biomedical Clinic franchise, establishing an international network dedicated to early detection, personalized health optimization, and integrative wellness. The model emphasizes the connection between mind, body, and environment, offering individuals a proactive approach to long-term health. TALK TITLE: INDIVIDUAL RESILIENCE TO SYSTEM SAFETY: THE VITAL SAFETY SYSTEM (VSS) INTRODUCTION: Across many sectors, organisations are experiencing rising levels of burnout, disengagement, ethical strain, and performance fragility. These challenges are frequently addressed by encouraging individuals to build resilience, despite consistent evidence that many of these pressures originate within organisational systems. In high-pressure environments, when systems fail to detect early warning signs or provide protective structures, the responsibility for managing risk is often placed on individuals. This creates unsustainable expectations and increases the likelihood of silent failure, ethical compromise, and burnout. AIM: The aim of this presentation is to explore the shift from individual resilience to system safety and to introduce the Vital Safety System (VSS), a preventative organisational framework designed to strengthen wellbeing, accountability, and sustainable performance at the system level. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The Vital Safety System was developed through the synthesis of real-world leadership experience in high-pressure environments, alongside established research in psychological safety, organisational governance, risk management, and human performance. The VSS framework integrates four core system layers: early risk awareness, protective governance, human-centred leadership practice, and sustainable performance design. Rather than replacing existing policies or wellbeing initiatives, the framework provides a structured approach that helps organisations identify emerging strain, support ethical decision-making, and respond proportionately to operational pressures. RESULTS: Implementation of the VSS framework enables organisations to detect risks earlier, reduce reliance on individual overextension, and strengthen trust between leaders and teams. By embedding safety, protection, and accountability within organisational systems, leaders can sustain performance while reducing the likelihood of burnout, disengagement, and reactive crisis management. CONCLUSION: The Vital Safety System (VSS) reframes wellbeing and performance as matters of organisational design rather than individual resilience. By shifting focus from personal coping strategies to system-level responsibility, organisations can protect people, strengthen trust, and sustain high performance in complex environments. VSS offers a practical framework for leaders seeking to build safer, more ethical, and future-ready organisations. KEYWORDS: Vital Safety System (VSS), System Safety, Psychological Safety, Human Performance Under Pressure, Preventative Organisational Design, System-Level Wellbeing, Ethical Risk Management, Protective Governance, Sustainable Performance, Leadership in High-Pressure Environments, Early Risk Detection, Human-Centred Leadership, Workforce Resilience vs System Responsibility, Trust and Accountability, Future-Ready Organisations Biography: Rebecca Hutchinson, ARRC is a systems-focused leader and framework designer working at the intersection of organisational safety, human performance, and future-ready governance. With a background spanning defence, healthcare, and complex operational environments, Rebecca has spent her career working inside systems where sustained pressure, ethical risk, and human cost are daily realities. Through this experience, she identified a recurring gap across sectors: organisations invest heavily in individual resilience while lacking structures that detect risk early and protect people at system level. She developed the Vital Safety System (VSS) to address this gap. VSS is a preventative organisational framework that integrates early risk awareness, protective governance, human-centred leadership, and sustainable performance into a single operating model. It is designed to work alongside existing strategies, data, and technologies, supporting organisations to perform under pressure without reliance on burnout or silent failure. Rebecca now works with leaders and organisations seeking to design systems that are safer, more ethical, and fit for the future of work. Rebecca Hutchinson Rebecca Hutchinson Director & Founder, Thrive Organisational Health | Creator of the Vital Safety System™ | Designing system-level interventions that protect human capacity and prevent burnout in high-pressure organisations

Mediterranean Therapy® emerges as a response to these challenges, offering a holistic travel-based well-being model inspired by the traditional Mediterranean way of living. Rooted in slow rhythms, social connection, nature, and nourishing food culture, the concept reframes travel as a supportive environment for inner renewal and personal transformation. AIM: Mediterranean Therapy® aims to explore how immersive, small-group travel experiences rooted in Mediterranean lifestyle principles can support emotional balance, self-reconnection, and personal growth. The program seeks to demonstrate that intentional travel, combined with cultural, sensory, and relational elements, can become a pathway to inner clarity and renewed vitality. MATERIALS : The Mediterranean Therapy® is delivered through structured retreat-style travel experiences hosted in a carefully selected luxury Mediterranean villa. Groups are limited to a maximum of 15 participants to ensure intimacy and personalized attention. The method combines: Guided reflective practices and gentle facilitation Shared cultural and nature-based experiences Slow-paced daily rhythms aligned with natural surroundings Community-building through shared presence and conversation Mindful engagement with food, environment, and local traditions Participants are supported through intentional moments of pause, connection, and self-observation, allowing inner processes to unfold naturally rather than through intensive intervention. Methods: The “materials” of Mediterranean Therapy® are experiential and environmental rather than clinical. They include: A Mediterranean villa setting that provides safety, beauty, and comfort Natural landscapes (sea, sun, gardens, fresh air) that encourage sensory regulation and relaxation Mediterranean gastronomy, including local, seasonal ingredients and shared meals Cultural elements such as local traditions, markets, and community interaction Facilitated group spaces for dialogue, reflection, and shared experience These elements act as supportive tools that create a restorative atmosphere and encourage emotional openness and inner alignment. RESULTS: Participants report lower stress, improved mood, and greater inner calm. The experience promotes emotional balance, mental clarity, and renewed life perspective. Shared meals and the small-group setting enhance connection, belonging, and overall well-being. Mediterranean Therapy® supports self- reconnection and emotional renewal through immersive, meaningful travel. CONCLUSION: Mediterranean Therapy® suggests that travel, when intentionally designed, can function as a holistic well-being intervention rather than mere leisure. By integrating environment, culture, nutrition, and human connection, the program supports emotional regulation, self-awareness, and renewed life perspective. This model highlights the therapeutic potential of slow, meaningful travel experiences and proposes a shift from consumption-based tourism toward transformation-oriented journeys that nurture long-term inner well-being. Brittany Smith Brittany Smith TALK TITLE: INTRODUCTION FOR MINDSET AND INNER NARRATIVE IN WOMEN’S LEADERSHIP INTRODUCTION: Women do not become powerful leaders by fixing what is broken — they become powerful by understanding the stories they have been carrying. The way a woman leads is shaped not only by her skills and experience, but by the beliefs, narratives, and identities she has formed along the way. This presentation explores the role of the mind in leadership and why the stories women tell themselves are instrumental in how they show up, take up space, and lead others. The approach shared in this session draws from mindset work, neuroscience, and mind–body awareness to help women recognize the narratives they lead from and reconnect with a more authentic, confident leadership identity—one that supports clarity, resilience, and sustainable impact. AIM: The aim of this session is to help women leaders recognize and transform the internal narratives that shape their leadership identity, confidence, and decision-making. By exploring mindset and mind–body awareness, the session supports women in releasing self-limiting patterns and leading with greater clarity, authenticity, and self-trust, while aligning their leadership presence with their values, wellbeing, and long-term impact. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The insights shared in this presentation are drawn from years of working closely with women through coaching, guided reflection, and embodied leadership practices. Through intentional conversations, reflective exercises, and lived leadership experiences, common themes began to emerge around self-doubt, over-responsibility, perfectionism, and the quiet ways women minimize themselves. These patterns were observed, reflected upon, and organized into core leadership themes that reveal how internal storytelling shapes external leadership behavior. Participation in this work was voluntary and grounded in trust, confidentiality, and personal agency. RESULTS: Women who became aware of their internal narratives experienced powerful shifts in how they led. Many reported increased confidence, clearer decision- making, stronger boundaries, and a deeper sense of self-trust. As old stories were questioned and rewritten, women found themselves speaking more freely, leading with greater presence, and allowing themselves to be seen without apology. However, the same visibility now feeds automated systems that profile and assess leadership credibility at scale—often placing women under disproportionate scrutiny. This makes digital presence not just a branding issue, but a leadership and governance imperative requiring strategic, informed engagement to ensure visibility expands opportunity rather than limits it. AIM / OBJECTIVE: This session aims to highlight the invisible data-related risks women leaders face in an AI-driven digital economy while showing how digital visibility can still be leveraged for business growth, inbound opportunity, and leadership influence. It provides practical frameworks to help women remain visible, credible, and effective without increasing exposure to reputational, security, or asset-related risks. By building awareness of how digital identity is profiled and interpreted by AI systems, the session empowers women to protect their reputation, safeguard trust, and sustain long-term leadership impact in a data- driven world. MATERIALS AND METHODS BY APPROACH: The session presents a structured, non-technical framework based on leadership practice, data governance principles, and real-world business experience. Key methods include: strategic digital visibility and content positioning to support inbound opportunity without revealing sensitive metadata or behavioral patterns; Digital hygiene and boundary setting to reduce identity, health, and reputational exposure; structural separation between public profiles and private assets to enhance safety and asset protection; and leadership participation in data governance through targeted questions, transparency requirements, and accountability mechanisms within organizations and vendor relationships. RESULTS / DISCUSSION: The application of these methods enables women leaders to maintain strong and strategic professional visibility while significantly reducing unnecessary digital and data-related risk. At the organizational level, these practices contribute to healthier data governance, more equitable and transparent decision- making, and improved trust across teams, partners, and stakeholders, ultimately supporting more sustainable leadership influence and long-term organizational integrity. CONCLUSION / SUMMARY: In an AI-driven world, visibility and protection are not opposing forces but complementary leadership responsibilities. Women leaders who approach data with strategic intent, governance awareness, and structural safeguards are better positioned to build sustainable businesses, protect their influence, and shape decision-making environments. Understanding and managing digital risk is no longer a technical concern; it is a core leadership competency essential for long-term success. Dr. Csilla Havas Dr. Csilla Havas Talk Title: “A művészet nem csak látható – megélhető. / Art is not only seen – it is lived.” INTRODUCTION: LullaCharm—Wearable Art is an innovative artistic fashion concept in which fine art transcends the traditional canvas and becomes a living, moving experience. Founded by painter and art manager Dr. Csilla Havas, who is also the founder and owner of the Havas Art Agency & Gallery, the brand explores the fusion of visual art and fashion design. Each garment originates from an original painting, transforming clothing into a personal and expressive work of art. LullaCharm is rooted in the philosophy that art should not remain static or confined to gallery walls but instead become part of everyday life and human expression. As the brand’s motto states: “Art is not only seen – it is lived.” AIM: The aim of LullaCharm – Wearable Art is to redefine how art is experienced by transforming original paintings into wearable designs that move with the human body. The project seeks to dissolve the boundary between fine art and fashion, allowing art to exist beyond gallery walls and become part of everyday life. Through this fusion of painting, textile design, and garment construction, LullaCharm aims to create a living artistic experience in which the wearer becomes an active participant in the artwork, embodying the belief that art is not only seen – it is lived. MATERIALS : LullaCharm – Wearable Art combines traditional fine art materials with modern textile and fashion design resources. Original artworks are created using professional paints and canvas, then digitized through high-resolution scanning and graphic software to preserve their visual integrity. These designs are printed onto carefully selected fabrics such as silk, satin, chiffon, and soft cotton blends that enhance movement and flow. Digital textile printing techniques, along with professional pattern-making and garment construction tools, are used to transform each painting into a high-quality, wearable piece of art. Methods: The creative process begins with the creation of an original painting, developed as an independent artwork with its own conceptual, emotional, and aesthetic narrative. These paintings are then digitally adapted and carefully translated onto textile surfaces, ensuring the integrity of color, composition, and artistic intention is preserved. Garment design is developed in harmony with the artwork, taking into consideration the natural movement and form of the female body. Fabric selection, cut, and drape are chosen to enhance the visual flow of the painting when worn, allowing the artwork to shift and come alive through motion. This interdisciplinary method merges fine art, digital technology, textile design, and fashion construction into a unified creative practice. RESULTS: The outcome of this process is a collection of garments that function simultaneously as fashion pieces and autonomous works of art. Each LullaCharm design carries the emotional depth and originality of a painting while gaining a new dimension through movement and personal embodiment. The wearer becomes an active participant in the artistic experience, transforming the perception of art from passive observation to lived interaction. The brand demonstrates that fashion can serve as a dynamic exhibition space, extending the life and reach of fine art beyond galleries and into everyday environments. CONCLUSION: LullaCharm redefines the boundaries between art and fashion by positioning the human body as a living canvas. Through the transformation of original paintings into wearable designs, the brand challenges conventional distinctions between static and dynamic art forms. This approach supports a more intimate, experiential relationship with art, aligning with the belief that art is not only meant to be viewed, but to be lived, felt, and moved in. Under the artistic direction of Dr. Csilla Havas, LullaCharm represents a contemporary model of how fine art can evolve into immersive, personal, and socially visible expression. KEYWORDS: Wearable Art, Art in Fashion, Interdisciplinary Design, Artistic Textiles, Body as Canvas, Contemporary Art, Experiential Art, Female Form in Art Biography: Dr. Csilla Havas is a painter, art manager, and cultural entrepreneur whose work is rooted in the belief that art is a living force—one that shapes dialogue, identity, and human connection. Aim: This presentation investigates whether learning diversity and inclusive education can serve as transformative pathways for developing entrepreneurial leadership in women challenging the persistent belief that leadership ability is purely innate. Introduction: In today’s innovation-driven world, as the traditional view of leadership as a fixed trait must be revised, the narrative of who can lead must also evolve. This view often excludes women in general and neurodivergent women in particular, especially those with learning differences such as dyslexia. This study proposes that inclusive and neurodiversity-informed educationcan be the innovative catalyst for developing women entrepreneurs. Drawing upon both practice and research, this presentation repositions learning challenges as untapped assets in the leadership development conversation. Materials and Methods: The qualitative study draws on observational data from over 30 female learners aged 10–18 across 6 schools in Cameroon, who received intervention using the Orton- Gillingham Structured Literacy approach. Grounded in a strengths-based model of neurodiversity, this method aimed not only at reading remediation but at developing transferable competencies such as criticalthinking, communication, and adaptability. Supplementing this practice, the study incorporates findings from The Dyslexic Advantage (Eide & Eide, 2011), and aligns with Howard Gardner’s theory of Multiple Intelligences and Vygotsky’s sociocultural learning theory both of which validate differentiated pathways to knowledge and leadership. Results: Post-intervention, students showed measurable increases in confidence, problem- solving, verbal reasoning, and creative risk-taking. These traits mirror established entrepreneurial competencies. Structured literacy did more than build reading skills—it provided a framework for students to understand how their unique thinking styles contribute to leadership and innovation. Conclusion: Leadership is not solely innate; it can be cultivated through intentional, inclusive education. When learning environments shift from deficit models to strengths- based approaches, particularly for neurodiverse learners, women previously excluded from entrepreneurial spaces begin to thrive. This inclusive imagination of leadership not only promotes equity but supports innovation, adaptability, and sustainable economic growth. Speaker Name: EnowBisong spouse Njonje Alice Bessem Talk Title: Born to Lead or Taught to Thrive? Can Learning Diversity and Inclusive Education be the Innovative Route to Reimagining Entrepreneurial Leadership for Women?

INTRODUCTION: Not even 100 years ago, women were forbidden from opening their own bank account. Women historically have been seen as being housewives, raising children and keeping the home in order while the man of the family worked supposedly harder than her and supported the family. However, during World Wars 1 and II, women entered the workplace to replace the men at war. In 1919, the Congressional Sexual Discrimination Removal Act was passed, and women were allowed to work in the legal industry or civil service. In 1968, the Equal Pay Act followed the first female walkout at work. In 1983, the Equal Pay Amendment resulted in women being allowed to earn the same as men when doing the same job. And in 1975, the Sex Discrimination Act made it illegal to discriminate against women in employment and education.[1] AIM: Bring about the understanding that women still experience some inequality in the workforce through being passed over for promotions and not being fully supported in their work. One example – an insurance company that gives the best “leads” to their men while woman have to make it on their own selling insurance. With approximately 43% of first marriages, 60% of second marriages and 73% of third marriages ending in divorce, it is no joke that both sexes – men and women – should know how to support themselves and that means, yes, equal pay for equal work.[2] MATERIALS AND METHODS BY APPROACH: For this key note I will work from prepared slides and engage the thought process of the audience with a few questions. RESULTS: Women have been in the workforce through necessity since World War I began in 1914.Now they are in the workforce by choice, some even switching roles in the family being the main breadwinner. And men are showing themselves to be very astute at raising children. These days with inflation and what is required to support and raise a family, at least two incomes are needed and it really doesn’t matter who brings in the money as long as it is coming in. CONCLUSION: Accepting women in the workforce with no hold-backs such as the “glass ceiling” is paramount to this world evolving and becoming the best it can be. Women not only have proven themselves educationally, but also in holding high-up positions in the corporate as well as governmental arenas. [1] “Women in the workforce: A timeline through the ages,” Thinkmoney, September 2021. [2] “Revealing Divorce Statistics in 2025,” Forbes, November 2025. INTRODUCTION: Leadership, often associated with power, influence, and identity, is traditionally shaped by masculine norms. However, gender plays a significant role in how leadership is expressed, perceived, and supported. Drawing on her extensive global experience in the hospitality and gaming industries, Dr. Manida Xongmixay Lau explores how gender-based expectations influence leadership behaviors and access to opportunities. The session addresses a critical question: does gender limit leadership capacity, or do societal perceptions and organizational culture define those limits? AIM: The session aims to explore the nuanced intersection between gender and leadership, breaking down stereotypes and comparing leadership styles typically labeled as “masculine” or “feminine.” It further seeks to present practical strategies to foster gender equity—both within organizations and at the individual level— empowering women to thrive in executive roles while reshaping what effective leadership looks like. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using an engaging and insightful PowerPoint presentation, Dr. Lau delivers: A comparative analysis of feminine (collaborative, emotionally intelligent, people-oriented) vs. masculine (decisive, risk-taking, performance-driven) leadership styles Real-life experiences and research-driven insights. An exploration of context-dependence, blended styles, and how leadership style is shaped by culture, industry, and personality Strategies at two levels: Organizational: Gender-neutral recruitment, inclusive work culture, mentorship programs, bias awareness Individual (Feminine leaders): Owning ambition, building influence, developing executive presence, and lifting others Audience interaction and reflective dialogue are used to challenge norms and provoke thought. RESULTS: The presentation reveals that diverse leadership teams—blending both masculine and feminine strengths—consistently achieve better creativity, problem-solving, and employee satisfaction. However, women often bear additional social and familial responsibilities that create unique pressures and perceptions in the workplace. These multiple “hats” can lead to burnout and limit upward mobility, not due to a lack of ability, but due to systemic expectations. Therefore, advancing gender equity in leadership requires both structural change and individual empowerment. CONCLUSION: Gender should not define leadership potential. Effective leadership transcends traditional gender labels, thriving instead on emotional intelligence, strategic thinking, and adaptability. Organizations must value diverse leadership styles, while women must be encouraged to lead authentically and boldly. As Dr. Lau concludes, the future of leadership depends on our collective willingness to dismantle stereotypes, redefine success, and create space for all voices—especially those long overlooked. Talk Title: The Intersection of Gender and Leadership Speaker Name: Dr. Manida Xongmixay Lau

Across developing and emerging economies, entrepreneurs hold immense potential to drive innovation, job creation, and long-term resilience, yet many remain excluded from global opportunity due to systemic barriers such as limited market access, fragmented ecosystems, and inequitable investment practices. As global economies become increasingly interconnected, leadership must evolve to foster inclusive entrepreneurial environments that enable participation across borders, cultures, and industries. Ethical investment, digital platforms, capacity building, and public–private collaboration are no longer optional mechanisms; they are essential enablers of sustainable development. When aligned effectively, these forces empower entrepreneurs not only to scale economically, but also to generate positive social and environmental outcomes. Scaling Humanity: The Leadership Shift Behind Sustainable Global Growth explores how human-centered leadership and globally connected ecosystems can unlock entrepreneurial potential while strengthening economic resilience. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The presentation integrates experiential storytelling, business case analysis, and leadership systems design. Method offers a practical roadmap for transforming overwhelm into sustainable success, making it a powerful tool for leaders across corporate and entrepreneurial landscapes. As a result, many high-achieving leaders experience burnout, identity dissonance, and ethical fatigue despite measurable accomplishments. This session introduces a reframed leadership lens that examines the emotional and cognitive forces shaping decision-making beneath the surface of achievement—specifically the overlooked role of regret in leadership behavior and long-term fulfillment. AIM: The aim of this session is to reframe fear and regret as critical data points in leadership decision-making, and to equip leaders with an integrated framework for navigating complexity with clarity, integrity, and courage—without sacrificing responsibility, ambition, or sustainability. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This session draws on a qualitative, integrative methodology combining: Over 25 years of executive advisory and leadership coaching experience across global sectors Doctoral research in global business and leadership Narrative inquiry and reflective practice Case-based insights from senior leaders navigating transition, burnout, and identity shifts A proprietary leadership framework (Fearless Living™) grounded in values alignment, ethical decision-making, and integrated resilience Participants engage through guided reflection, conceptual reframing, and practical application rather than didactic instruction. RESULTS: Participants gain heightened awareness of the often-unexamined ways fear subtly shapes leadership behavior, risk assessment, communication patterns, and decision-making processes. Rather than viewing fear as a liability, leaders learn to recognize it as a diagnostic signal—revealing misalignment between values, identity, and action. CONCLUSION: Leadership in the modern world demands more than competence and courage—it demands coherence. When leaders align who they are with how they lead, they cultivate cultures of trust, innovation, and resilience that extend far beyond individual performance metrics. These early experiences often contribute to anxiety, depression, attachment challenges, and maladaptive coping strategies later in life. Purposeful parenting presents a proactive and emotionally responsive approach to interrupt these patterns and support healthy emotional development. AIM: This presentation aims to introduce Purposeful Parenting as a trauma-informed framework and to demonstrate how the L.O.V.E. method—Listen, Observe, Validate, and Express—can nurture emotional intelligence, strengthen parent–child relationships, and prevent the intergenerational transmission of emotional trauma.By emphasizing emotional attunement and conscious communication, the presentation explores how the L.O.V.E. method helps caregivers recognize and respond to children’s emotional needs with empathy rather than reactivity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The L.O.V.E. method was applied as a practical parenting intervention emphasizing intentional emotional attunement and communication. The framework integrates principles from emotional intelligence research, attachment theory, and trauma-informed care. Each component—active listening, non-verbal observation, emotional validation, and healthy emotional expression—was implemented through real-life parenting scenarios, reflective practices, and modeled communication strategies designed to enhance emotional awareness and regulation in children. RESULTS: Application of the L.O.V.E. method demonstrated improved emotional expression, increased emotional safety, stronger attachment bonds, and enhanced self-regulation in children. Caregivers reported reduced behavioral reactivity, improved communication, and greater emotional resilience within family systems. Children showed increased self-confidence, emotional vocabulary, and adaptive coping skills. Additionally, children demonstrated higher levels of self-confidence, expanded emotional vocabulary, and improved adaptive coping strategies when facing stress, disappointment, or frustration. These outcomes suggest that early emotional attunement through the L.O.V.E. method supports CONCLUSION: Purposeful parenting using the L.O.V.E. method offers an effective, accessible approach to fostering emotional intelligence and resilience in children. By addressing emotional needs early and intentionally, caregivers can prevent the development of trauma-related coping mechanisms and support children in becoming emotionally secure, compassionate, and confident adults. This approach empowers parents with practical tools to respond rather than react, strengthening trust and emotional safety within the family. Over time, consistent use of the L.O.V.E. method nurtures healthy communication, self-regulation, and empathy. Ultimately, it helps break intergenerational cycles of trauma and builds a foundation for lifelong wellbeing and strong relationships. Talk Title: Self-Acceptance, Emotional Courage & Personal Growth in a High-Pressure World: Lessons for Sustainable Inner Leadership NTRODUCTION: In an increasingly fast-paced and performance-driven world, individuals are often encouraged to pursue external achievements while neglecting internal wellbeing. This imbalance can lead to burnout, identity confusion, and emotional disconnection. Increasingly, research and lived experience suggest that sustainable success begins with self-acceptance, emotional awareness, and the courage to confront personal fears (Ghanem, 2024). Personal development is not a linear process. Many individuals believe they must first achieve confidence before acting, when in reality confidence frequently develops through consistent action, self-reflection, and compassionate self-understanding (Ghanem, 2024). AIM: This keynote aims to: 1. Highlight the importance of self-acceptance as the foundation of authentic growth. 2. Explore how fear, self-doubt, and emotional resistance prevent individuals from becoming their best selves. 3. Encourage participants to cultivate self-respect, emotional resilience, and sustainable personal leadership. 4. Inspire deeper conversations about mental wellbeing, authenticity, and purposeful living. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This session combines reflective storytelling and lived personal insights with guided self-reflection questions for the audience. It integrates coaching frameworks centered on emotional awareness and mindset shifts, along with interactive discussions designed to normalize vulnerability and personal growth. Self-Acceptance as Foundation Self-acceptance does not mean complacency; rather, it creates psychological safety from which genuine growth can occur. When individuals accept their current reality, they reduce internal resistance and increase clarity about future change (Ghanem, 2024). 2. Fear as a Growth Barrier Fear often manifests subtly fear of judgment, failure, rejection, or inadequacy. Many individuals attempt self-love practices while unconsciously avoiding these deeper fears. Addressing fear directly is often the turning point toward personal transformation (Ghanem, 2024). 3. Emotional Courage and Authentic Leadership Authenticity requires emotional courage. Leaders, creators, and professionals who embrace vulnerability often demonstrate stronger resilience, better relationships, and more sustainable performance outcomes. 4.Sustainable personal growth requires consistency over perfection, compassion over self-criticism, awareness over avoidance, and alignment between values, actions, and identity. CONCLUSION: Developing self-acceptance, self-respect, and emotional resilience is a lifelong journey rather than a fixed destination. Sustainable growth emerges when individuals: 1. Acknowledge fears honestly. 2. Practice ongoing self-reflection and compassion. 3. Build emotional awareness alongside professional ambition. 4. Commit to authentic self-expression and aligned living. Ultimately, becoming one’s best self is less about perfection and more about courage, awareness, and continuous growth (Ghanem, 2024). Daryna Martynenko Daryna Martynenko Talk Title: Coaching for Agentic Leadership: A Social Cognitive Approach to Navigating Irreversible Change and Uncertainty INTRODUCTION: Irreversible change often disrupts leaders' perceived control, resulting in victim positioning and diminished agency. While coaching is widely applied in crisis contexts, underlying social-cognitive mechanisms remain under-articulated. This study examines how coaching processes activate self-efficacy and agentic self-regulation when external circumstances are unchangeable. AIM: To explore how coaching interventions grounded in Social Cognitive Theory facilitate shifts toward agentic leadership functioning under conditions of irreversible organizational or societal change, with particular attention to the role of acceptance in restoring perceived agency. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This exploratory qualitative study draws on coaching practice conducted between 2022 and 2025 with business leaders experiencing complex or high-stakes transitions in conditions of sustained uncertainty. Data sources include anonymized coaching session notes and reflective documentation. Using a deductive thematic analysis guided by Bandura's agency framework, cognitive and behavioral shifts were examined in relation to the four sources of self-efficacy (mastery experience, vicarious learning, verbal persuasion, affective regulation) and the core features of personal agency (intentionality, forethought, self-regulation, self-reflectiveness). The study employs analytic generalization rather than statistical inference and does not aim to establish causal relationships. RESULTS: Recurring patterns indicate transitions from constraint-oriented narratives toward intentionality, reflection, and adaptive planning. Leaders accepting irreversibility demonstrated accelerated agentic restoration compared to those maintaining resistance. Shifts align with Social Cognitive Theory mechanisms: mastery recall, cognitive reframing, and self-regulatory redirection toward controllable domains. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that coaching can be conceptualized as a structured social-cognitive process supporting agentic leadership under conditions of uncertainty or crisis. Acceptance of unchangeable circumstances may function as a facilitating mechanism rather than a barrier to agency restoration. The contribution is interpretive and theoretical rather than causal. Coaching practitioners may benefit from explicitly integrating acceptance processes with agency-building interventions. Further empirical research using controlled longitudinal designs is necessary to test predictive validity and examine mediating mechanisms. KEYWORDS: Leadership coaching, Social Cognitive Theory, self-efficacy, personal agency, acceptance, crisis leadership Biography: Daryna Martynenko is an ICF‑accredited professional coach who empowers leaders, managers, and entrepreneurs to navigate complex environments with clarity, resilience, and adaptive agency. She supports decision-makers in moving from uncertainty to actionable insight and confident choices. In her work, Daryna facilitates mindset shifts, guiding clients to develop new perspectives, greater self-awareness, and adaptive thinking. She integrates research-backed strategies with practical guidance to unlock potential and cultivate effective leadership. Committed to helping people align their strengths, values, and aspirations, she enables clients to live and lead with purpose, authenticity, and full realization. Executive Coach ICF and Business Trainer

Stephanie O'Brien Stephanie O'Brien Talk Title: The Business Athlete: A Playbook for Clarity, Courage, and Compounding Impact. Introduction: Leadership in contemporary organizations often suffers from reactive decision-making, fragmented priorities, and burnout-driven execution. Drawing from principles of elite athletic performance, The Business Athlete framework positions leadership as a disciplined, trainable practice rather than a reactive role. It emphasizes consistency, reflection, and courageous action to help leaders build focus, resilience, and clarity under pressure. Designed for founder-led and growth-stage organizations, the framework enables sustainable performance, aligned execution, and repeatable results over time. AIM: This session introduces the Business Athlete framework and the Leadership Loop as a practical and repeatable model for strengthening leadership effectiveness and driving sustained organizational performance. It explores how leaders can shift from reactive decision-making to disciplined, intentional leadership by building consistency, self-awareness, and courageous execution. Through the Leadership Loop, participants will learn how continuous reflection, aligned action, and feedback create momentum, resilience, and clarity, enabling leaders to navigate complexity, reduce burnout, and deliver consistent results in dynamic business environments. Materials and Methods: The framework is derived from applied coaching experience across sport and business contexts, translating proven athletic training principles into leadership and organizational practices. Concepts such as performance cycles, cadence, recovery, and feedback loops are adapted to help leaders structure their work with greater focus and consistency. The approach emphasizes structured commitments, reflective routines, and disciplined conversations to improve accountability, decision quality, and team alignment, supporting sustained performance over time. By integrating both physical and cognitive performance strategies, the framework ensures holistic development and long-term organizational resilience. Results: Application of the Leadership Loop leads to improved strategic clarity, more consistent execution, and stronger accountability within teams. Organizations report cleaner decision-making processes, reclaimed leadership time, reduced operational noise, and healthier team dynamics without increased burnout. Performance gains are achieved through repeatable systems rather than short-term motivation. Leaders also develop greater foresight and adaptability, as structured feedback loops allow them to anticipate challenges and adjust strategies proactively. Over time, teams build a shared language and rhythm around priorities, enhancing collaboration, trust, and resilience across the organization, ultimately creating a sustainable culture of high performance and continuous improvement. CONCLUSION: Leadership excellence is not accidental; it is the result of deliberate practice and disciplined systems. Treating leadership as an athletic pursuit shifts it from a reactive, personality-driven activity to a structured and trainable discipline, enabling organizations to translate strategy into consistent execution. This approach replaces noise with rhythm and intention with measurable action. The Business Athlete framework provides a repeatable playbook that aligns decision-making and performance through cadence and feedback. Leaders develop clarity in priorities, courage in conversations, and accountability in outcomes. Over time, effort compounds through reflection and learning rather than motivation alone. The result is predictable, sustainable growth supported by healthier teams and resilient leaders capable of delivering repeatable results. Rachael Richardson Rachael Richardson Talk Title: Why Life Experience Is the Best Work Experience: Implications for Workforce Development, Equity, and Health Outcomes INTRODUCTION: Workforce systems continue to privilege formal credentials, excluding workers with lived experience despite evidence that socio-emotional and relational skills drive labor-market performance (Heckman & Kautz, 2012). Globally, an estimated 54% of employers report soft skills shortages (WEF, 2023), while 92% of hiring managers consider soft skills equally or more important than technical skills (LinkedIn, 2022). Concurrently, employment is recognized as a core social determinant of health influencing morbidity, mortality, and well-being (Marmot, 2015; WHO, 2014). AIM: To validate life experience as a legitimate and valuable form of work experience; to illustrate how lived expertise broadens and strengthens equitable workforce participation—particularly for women, caregivers, and historically marginalized groups; and to examine the downstream impacts of recognizing lived experience on public health outcomes, economic stability, and community well-being. This approach highlights how inclusive definitions of expertise can reduce systemic barriers, enhance workforce resilience, and contribute to more responsive, human-centered policy and organizational practices. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Interdisciplinary literature synthesis drawing from psychology, labor economics, public health, and re-entry studies; qualitative case evidence derived from justice-involved and system-impacted populations; and comparative competency analysis examining skills, capacities, and outcomes associated with lived-experience pathways versus traditional credential-based models. Together, these approaches illuminate how experiential knowledge translates into workforce readiness, leadership capability, and social impact across diverse employment and re-entry contexts. RESULTS: Analysis indicates that lived experience generates competencies in resilience, communication, problem solving, and cultural intelligence. For justice- involved individuals, employment reduces recidivism by 20–50% (Couloute & Kopf, 2018; NASEM, 2022) and increases lifetime earnings—both associated with improved health trajectories. Increased employment stability reduces depressive symptoms and improves self-efficacy (Dooley et al., 2012). Economic mobility is strongly predictive of life expectancy, with each upward income quintile associated with 4.5–8.5 additional years of life. (Chetty et al., 2016). In service fields, lived experience practitioners improve engagement and treatment adherence, yielding 20–30% higher retention rates in behavioral health and harm reduction interventions (SAMHSA, 2020). These findings suggest that recognizing lived expertise not only enhances equity and organizational effectiveness but also produces population-level health benefits. CONCLUSION: Life experience is not ancillary to work, but a legitimate and essential form of employability that generates transferable skills, adaptive capacity, and contextual intelligence. When formally recognized and integrated into workforce systems, lived experience strengthens key social determinants of health— including economic stability, social inclusion, and access to opportunity—while reducing structural inequities. Valuing life experience as employability capital supports healthier individuals, more resilient communities, and more effective, equity-centered labor and public health outcomes. This recognition transforms barriers into assets, empowering individuals to convert adversity into leadership, purpose, and meaningful participation in the workforce and society. KEYWORDS: Trauma-informed care; community empowerment; systems change; restorative justice; prevention; wraparound services; peer support; advocacy; capacity building; inclusive leadership; policy reform; cross-sector collaboration; youth development; f stabilization; cultural competence; mental wellness Biography: Rachael Richardson is a workforce development strategist, social impact practitioner, and community advocate committed to advancing equity, re-entry employment, and economic mobility. With over a decade of experience across human services, entrepreneurship, and community leadership — and informed by lived experience — she designs workforce systems that recognize life experience as valuable talent and create stronger pathways to opportunity. Her work supports youth, justice-involved individuals, and underserved communities through trauma-informed, community-based solutions that improve social and economic outcomes. A recognized leader and award recipient, co-author of Faith Is, and speaker at state, national, civic, and faith-based forums, Rachael remains dedicated to redefining success and creating lasting change — one life, one job, and one opportunity at a time. 🌟 Executive Assistant | Workforce Development Specialist | Reentry Advocate | Faith-Based Leader | Hope Dealer
