Toni Curtis Toni Curtis Talk Title: “Beyond Depletion: How Endocrine Disorder, Infertility, and Postpartum Survival Gave Birth to the Physiological Birth Model” Introduction: For years, I was told my symptoms—fatigue, irregular cycles, hair loss, inflammation, and infertility—were “normal.” After conceiving, I was told that postpartum anemia, hemorrhage, delayed recovery, and emotional exhaustion were simply part of motherhood. They were not. Living with hypothyroidism and infertility, I encountered a healthcare system that treated symptoms in isolation while ignoring the connections between hormones, nutrition, stress, and recovery. Even as a doula, childbirth educator, and lactation counselor, I found myself dismissed and depleted, struggling to heal and trust my body again. This keynote is rooted in lived physiology and a new framework that honors the body’s intelligence. From this journey, the Physiological Birth Model was born. AIM: The aim of this keynote is to humanize endocrine disorder, infertility, and postpartum complications while demonstrating how restoration is possible when physiology is supported rather than overridden. This keynote seeks to: Reframe infertility and postpartum complications as interconnected physiological responses Highlight how epigenetically informed nutrition supports endocrine function and fertility Challenge the normalization of postpartum depletion Introduce the Physiological Birth Model as a restorative, nutrition-first framework grounded in lived healing Materials and Methods: This keynote is delivered through prepared slides, first-person narrative, and applied physiological explanation. The approach integrates: Lived experience with hypothyroidism, infertility, postpartum hemorrhage, anemia, hair loss, and lactation challenges Endocrine physiology and stress biology Epigenetics and gene expression influenced by nutrition and environment Nutritional therapy focused on bioavailability, absorption, and hormonal signaling Nervous system regulation and trauma-informed care Results: Through targeted, epigenetically informed nutrition, I supported endocrine function, restored nutrient sufficiency, and reduced chronic stress, allowing me to conceive naturally. After birth, long-term depletion appeared as blood loss, anemia, hair loss, and delayed recovery, while conventional care treated symptoms rather than systems. Healing required restoring hormonal regulation, digestion, nutrient absorption, thyroid support, and nervous system safety, enabling sustained lactation and restored fertility. This recovery became the foundation of the Physiological Birth Model, reframing nutrition, stress, and postpartum recovery as central to reproductive health. CONCLUSION: This keynote is a testament to what becomes possible when we stop asking bodies to endure and start supporting them to recover. The Physiological Birth Model emerged from the intersection of endocrine disorder, infertility, postpartum depletion, and restoration, calling for a fundamental shift—from symptom management to system repair, and from normalization of suffering to intentional nourishment. The session invites participants to reimagine care through a restorative, whole-body lens that honors the interconnected nature of hormones, metabolism, nervous system regulation, and emotional well- being. By weaving together clinical insight and lived experience, the keynote underscores that true healing requires time, education, and compassionate, individualized support rather than quick fixes. This paradigm challenges conventional narratives in women’s health and recovery, empowering individuals and professionals to advocate for care models that prioritize long-term vitality, sustainable energy, and genuine physiological resilience. KEYWORDS: Hypothyroidism, infertility, epigenetics, postpartum hemorrhage, anemia, lactation, endocrine health, physiological birth, postpartum recovery, nutrition, depletion, nervous system regulation, maternal healing, fertility restoration, intergenerational health Biography: Toni Curtis is a doula, childbirth educator, lactation counselor, nutritional therapist, and perinatal health advocate with over 30 years of experience. She is the founder of BirthWise Doula Services and creator of the Physiological Birth Model—a nutrition-first framework integrating endocrine health, stress physiology, and postpartum recovery to support long-term maternal wellbeing. Blending clinical expertise with lived experience, Toni addresses the root causes of maternal depletion and hormonal imbalance. She has trained and mentored perinatal professionals across six countries, advancing evidence-informed, nutrition-centered maternal care. Individuals begin to trust the rhythm of their own becoming, understanding that pauses, detours, and even breakdowns are often acts of redirection rather than failure. In this space of renewal and alignment, a profound truth reveals itself: what is meant for us does not pass us by—it meets us precisely when we are ready to receive it. The modern workplace has normalized reactivity, multitasking, and urgency as markers of competence, yet neuroscience tells a different story: chronic urgency erodes focus, diminishes emotional regulation, and compromises strategic thinking. This keynote introduces a counterintuitive yet evidence-based leadership advantage: the pause. Far from passivity, the pause is a deliberate neurological reset that restores clarity, presence, and executive functioning. Drawing from neuroscience, performance psychology, and high-stakes leadership environments, Dr. R. Harrison Baxter presents Reflective Leadership as a critical skill for leaders navigating complexity, uncertainty, and burnout. Central to this talk is the Intraflexion™ Model and the R³™ Methodology (Reflect → Respond → Rise) —a practical framework that teaches leaders how to interrupt reactive patterns, access internal certainty, and lead with precision rather than pressure. The keynote challenges a prevailing leadership myth: that faster decisions create better outcomes. Instead, it demonstrates that leadership excellence begins where reactivity ends. AIM: To equip leaders, executives, and decision-makers with a science-backed framework that builds internal certainty, restores focus, and creates psychologically safe environments — even in the face of chaos. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Neuroscience of Attention Deficit Trait (ADT) Task Positive Network & Default Mode Network activation The R³™ Methodology Real-time reflection and clarity techniques Case studies: Navy SEALs, C-suite leaders, global organizations RESULTS: By the conclusion of the session, attendees report a fundamental shift in how they experience leadership pressure. Key outcomes include: Improved focus and reduced mental fatigue Greater emotional regulation and stress resilience Clearer decision-making under pressure Enhanced psychological safety and trust within teams A leadership presence grounded in calm authority rather than urgency The discussion reframes leadership not as relentless output, but as intentional influence. Dr. Deitra C. Payne Dr. Deitra C. Payne Talk Title: “Power Redefined: How Empathetic Leadership Drives Measurable Impact” Introduction: For decades, leadership has been defined by control, dominance, and emotional detachment—a model rooted in hierarchical and militaristic traditions. While this paradigm once supported stability, it is increasingly ineffective in addressing today’s complex global challenges such as technological disruption, organizational change, crisis management, and workforce disengagement. Modern research reveals a growing disconnect between traditional leadership traits—overconfidence, dominance, and emotional suppression—and organizational effectiveness. In contrast, qualities often dismissed as “soft skills,” including empathy, emotional intelligence, collaboration, and transparency, have emerged as critical drivers of performance. This dismissal is deeply gendered, as relational leadership traits often associated with women are undervalued, despite evidence showing they are essential competencies for leading in complexity and achieving sustainable organizational success. AIM: The primary aim of this work is to demonstrate, through empirical research and organizational evidence, that empathetic leadership produces measurably stronger outcomes than traditional dominance-based leadership models. It seeks to challenge conventional power-driven leadership paradigms while presenting research that highlights the effectiveness of empathy, emotional intelligence, and collaboration in driving performance. The work also explores the “soft skills, hard results” paradox, identifying barriers that limit the adoption of empathetic leadership approaches. Additionally, it provides practical, actionable frameworks designed to help organizations successfully implement empathetic leadership and foster more sustainable, inclusive, and effective workplace cultures. Materials and Methods: This presentation uses a research-based approach, synthesizing peer-reviewed studies, organizational data, and leadership case analyses, delivered through PowerPoint slides. Results: Findings confirm that emotional intelligence and relational skills account for a significantly greater portion of leadership effectiveness than cognitive ability or technical expertise alone. Psychological safety emerges as the strongest predictor of team performance, while fear-based leadership suppresses innovation and adaptability. During crises, empathetic leadership—grounded in transparency and accountability—builds trust and produces superior outcomes compared to dominance-based approaches. Organizations practicing empathetic leadership demonstrate higher financial performance, increased innovation, stronger employee engagement and retention, greater crisis resilience, and enhanced customer loyalty. Despite these benefits, adoption remains limited due to measurement gaps, gender- based bias, and institutional systems that reward traditional power models. These barriers can be addressed through validated metrics, cultural reframing, and leadership system reform. CONCLUSION: The research establishes that traditional dominance-based leadership is no longer sufficient in today’s complex organizational environments. Empathetic leadership is not a soft alternative—it is a strategic imperative that delivers measurable, sustainable results. Empathy-driven leadership enhances performance across financial, human, and operational dimensions, and the skills required are learnable, scalable, and adaptable. Organizations that fail to evolve their leadership paradigms risk stagnation, disengagement, and diminished impact, while those that embrace empathetic leadership position themselves for long-term success. KEYWORDS: Empathetic Leadership, Emotional Intelligence (EQ), Psychological Safety, Leadership Effectiveness, Trust-Based Leadership, Collaborative Decision- Making, Evidence-Based Leadership,Transformation, Sustainable Leadership, Innovation, Crisis Leadership, Employee Engagement, Customer Loyalty. Marcia Blane Marcia Blane Talk Title: “Birthing Women Leadership:From Gestation to Greatness” Introduction: Despite women comprising a significant proportion of the global healthcare and service workforce, their representation in leadership remains disproportionately low. Structural inequities, implicit bias, and psychological barriers continue to hinder women’s leadership advancement. Contemporary research highlights women’s strengths in transformational leadership; however, supportive frameworks that address both individual development and organizational responsibility remain limited. AIM: The primary aim of this study is to conceptualize and present the Birthing Women Leadership: From Gestation to Greatness framework as a holistic, trauma-informed model for women’s leadership development. The framework seeks to (1) reframe leadership emergence as an embodied and developmental process, (2) identify critical psychological and structural challenges across leadership stages, and (3) emphasize organizational accountability in creating environments that sustain women leaders beyond role attainment. Materials and Methods: A conceptual and integrative methodology was employed, drawing upon psychological theory, trauma-informed leadership practices, organizational leadership research. Empirical evidence from global health, leadership studies, and workforce equity reports was synthesized to map leadership development phases onto a gestational model: conception, trimesters of growth, labor, birth, and postpartum leadership integration. Results: Women’s leadership development follows a nonlinear, developmental trajectory influenced by psychological readiness, organizational culture, and systemic access to opportunity rather than competency alone. Early leadership phases are characterized by identity formation, internal value alignment, and imposter syndrome, often intensified by limited representation and lack of visible role models. Mid-stage leadership development shows significant growth in communication, negotiation, emotional intelligence, and relational leadership capacity, aligning strongly with transformational leadership competencies. Advanced leadership stages are associated with increased visibility, performance scrutiny, and bias, resulting in heightened emotional labor and role strain. Lack of structured support during leadership transitions increases the risk of burnout, disengagement, and leadership attrition, particularly during high- responsibility phases. Organizations implementing mentorship, sponsorship, equitable promotion practices, and wellness-aligned leadership policies report higher leadership retention and stronger organizational outcomes. CONCLUSION: Women’s leadership development requires holistic, stage-specific frameworks that integrate psychological, emotional, and structural dimensions. The Birthing Women Leadership framework effectively reframes leadership emergence as an embodied, adaptive process, rather than a linear progression of skills. Addressing leadership inequity demands organizational accountability, not solely individual resilience or capability. Trauma-informed and wellness-aligned leadership ecosystems are essential for sustaining women leaders beyond role attainment. Sustainable women’s leadership contributes to long-term cultural transformation, equity, and inclusive governance. The framework provides actionable insights for organizations committed to advancing gender-equitable leadership systems. KEYWORDS: Women’s Leadership Development; Transformational Leadership; Trauma-Informed Leadership; Gender Equity; Organizational Culture; Leadership Sustainability; Embodied Leadership; Inclusive Leadership Systems Biography: Marcia Blane is a Licensed Professional Counselor, Certified Life Coach, author, and motivational speaker dedicated to empowering individuals through self-discovery and purposeful living. Catia Arnaut Catia Arnaut Talk Title: From Capitalism to Happytalism: A New Development Paradigm INTRODUCTION: In an era characterized by rapid economic globalization, escalating international conflicts, accelerating environmental degradation, and the deepening of social and economic inequalities, traditional measures of national progress are proving increasingly inadequate. For decades, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) has been the dominant indicator used to assess a nation’s success, offering a narrow view focused primarily on economic output and market activity. While GDP remains a valuable tool for measuring economic performance, it fails to capture the lived experiences of individuals, the quality of social relationships, environmental sustainability, mental and physical health, and the overall sense of meaning and satisfaction within societies. Consequently, GDP often overlooks the very elements that define human well-being and long-term societal resilience. Aim: This research seeks to explore alternative development paradigms that move beyond Gross Domestic Product (GDP), acknowledging that economic growth alone is no longer a sufficient or meaningful measure of national progress. While GDP captures market activity and financial performance, it overlooks critical dimensions of societal health such as social cohesion, environmental sustainability, mental and physical well-being, and the overall quality of life experienced by citizens. In response to these limitations, the study aims to identify the most influential national well-being indicators that more accurately reflect how societies function, thrive, and sustain themselves within an increasingly interconnected, uncertain, and complex global context. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This research adopts a comprehensive dashboard approach to the measurement of national well-being, drawing upon a broad set of internationally recognized well-being indicators developed by leading global institutions and research bodies. These indicators encompass economic, social, environmental, institutional, and psychological dimensions of societal functioning, allowing for a multidimensional assessment of national progress. To determine the relative importance of each indicator, rigorous statistical analysis was applied to examine their individual and collective influence on overall societal well-being. This analytical process enabled the identification of those variables that exert the strongest impact on well-being outcomes at the national level. RESULTS: The results of the analysis demonstrate that national well-being can be effectively captured through a significantly reduced yet robust set of ten core indicators. Despite the multidimensional nature of well-being, the findings reveal that these ten variables account for the most substantial influence on overall societal well-being, making extensive and complex dashboards unnecessary for meaningful assessment. Among these indicators, five were identified as having a positive influence on societal well-being, contributing directly to improved quality of life, social stability, and human flourishing, while the remaining five were found to exert a negative influence, acting as constraints or risk factors that diminish well-being outcomes.Building on these empirical findings, the study introduces a simplified and balanced measurement framework termed the Well-Being Balanced Scorecard (WBBS). The WBBS integrates both positive and negative drivers of well-being into a single, coherent structure, offering a clear and comprehensive overview of a nation’s well-being performance. By balancing enabling and inhibiting factors, the framework provides policymakers and stakeholders with an accessible tool for diagnosing well-being challenges, monitoring progress over time, and informing strategic decision-making aimed at enhancing societal resilience and sustainable development. CONCLUSION: This research confirms that Gross Domestic Product alone is an incomplete measure of national progress. While useful for assessing economic activity, GDP fails to capture essential aspects of human experience such as well-being, social cohesion, environmental sustainability, and quality of life. As global challenges grow more complex, relying solely on economic indicators risks undermining long-term resilience and prosperity. To address these gaps, the Well-Being Balanced Scorecard (WBBS) offers a practical, evidence-based framework that integrates happiness and well-being into national policy assessment. By balancing positive and negative well-being drivers, the WBBS enables policymakers to move beyond measurement toward action, supporting more inclusive, sustainable, and people-centered development strategies. KEYWORDS: This work focuses on national well-being, happiness economics, beyond GDP measurement, public policy, sustainable development, and balanced scorecard approaches. Biography: Catia Arnaut is an internationally recognized Happiness and Well-Being Researcher, Author, Entrepreneur, and Keynote Speaker, widely known for her work at the intersection of economics, globalization, and human-centered development. Her academic journey reflects a deep and multidisciplinary commitment to understanding well-being beyond traditional economic indicators. She holds an MSc in Economics, an MBA in Management and Strategic Planning, and a Master’s degree in Project Management, culminating in a PhD in Globalization Studies. Her doctoral research was dedicated to the study of national-level well-being, exploring alternative models for measuring societal progress beyond Gross Domestic Product and highlighting happiness and quality of life as essential dimensions of sustainable development . Happiness & Well-Being Researcher | Author | Chief Happiness Officer (CHO) | Entrepreneur | International Keynote Speaker

Param Sandhu Gill Param Sandhu Gill Talk Title: Intention-Based Mindfulness in Today’s World Introduction: Intentional mindfulness refers to the practice of mindfulness guided by a clear inner purpose such as compassion, wisdom, and non-harm, rather than treating mindfulness as a neutral relaxation technique or productivity tool. In today’s fast-paced and performance-driven culture, mindfulness is often reduced to what is referred to as “McMindfulness,” a self-centered optimization strategy. True intention-based mindfulness emphasizes that mindfulness is not just noticing, but noticing with direction—guided by values such as kindness, ethical awareness, and understanding. AIM: The objective of this session is to highlight the importance of intention in mindfulness practice and to demonstrate how ethical grounding transforms mindfulness from a stress-management tool into a practice that reshapes our relationship with ourselves and others. Materials and Methods: The session will be delivered as a reflective and experiential talk, inviting participants to engage actively with the concepts rather than passively receiving information. Drawing from traditional mindfulness teachings, contemporary scientific research, and real-life experiences, the presentation will provide a rich, multidimensional perspective on the practice of mindfulness. The discussion will explore how intention shapes awareness, guiding attention toward what is meaningful rather than merely what is measurable or externally validated. Participants will learn how cultivating mindfulness with purpose supports a sustainable and deeply fulfilling practice, allowing them to navigate daily challenges with clarity, resilience, and ethical grounding. Through a combination of guided reflections, illustrative examples, and interactive exercises, attendees will leave with practical tools to integrate intention-driven mindfulness into their personal and professional lives, creating space for calm, focus, and authentic growth. Results: Participants will gain a deep understanding of how intention-based mindfulness fosters a more profound and sustainable practice compared to outcome- driven approaches that focus primarily on performance or measurable results. The session will explore the distinction between practicing mindfulness with genuine intention versus practicing it as a tool for productivity, highlighting how the latter can lead to a spiritually hollow or misapplied practice. Special emphasis will be placed on the unique challenges faced by women in today’s fast-paced, multitasking world—navigating professional and personal roles, meeting societal expectations, and dealing with constant comparison and judgment. The discussion will provide practical strategies to integrate mindfulness into daily life in a way that is ethically grounded, personally fulfilling, and resilient, empowering participants to cultivate inner steadiness amidst external demands. Attendees will leave the session with actionable insights and tools to practice mindfulness with intention, enhance focus, reduce stress, and embrace a more meaningful and balanced approach to life, work, and personal growth. CONCLUSION: Intention-based mindfulness is a quiet yet powerful way of living deliberately in alignment with one’s inner truth and shared ethical values. Rather than focusing on productivity or outcomes, this practice is conscious, values-driven, and reflective, helping reduce harm, cultivate compassion, and build emotional resilience amid the pressures and pace of modern life. Through purposeful awareness, individuals develop greater sensitivity to their own needs and those of others, supporting empathy, ethical decision-making, and thoughtful engagement in both personal and professional settings. Intention-based mindfulness transforms everyday moments into opportunities for clarity, connection, and meaningful action, empowering people to live with greater alignment, authenticity, and lasting impact. KEYWORDS: Intention-based mindfulness, ethical awareness, compassion, women empowerment, self-development, non-harm, conscious living. Laurence THOMAS Laurence THOMAS Talk Title: Leading from the Space Just Before – Awakening Presence, Developing Impact INTRODUCTION: Contemporary organisational environments often privilege speed, immediacy and constant responsiveness. Yet research in contemplative sciences, cognitive psychology and leadership studies highlights the value of transitional or liminal moments — the brief interval preceding action, speech or decision-making (when the swimmer is about to plung or the sprinter awaiting the signal). This “Space Just Before” corresponds to a moment of embodied anticipation, where cognitive, emotional and attentional processes can be intentionally regulated. Comparable notions are found across contemplative traditions, artistic performance practices and creative disciplines, all recognising the generative potential of this pre-action pause. This presentation examines this threshold as a locus of agency, alignment and possibility, if we learn to inhabit it. AIM: The purpose of this presentation is to investigate how cultivating awareness in the “Space Just Before” enhances leadership effectiveness. Developing the capacity to pause before reacting facilitates a shift from habitual, automatic responses toward more deliberate, context-sensitive choices. This reflective stance supports discernment, mitigates cognitive biases and expands perceived options for action. Cultivating awareness of the « Space Just Before” strengthens our capacity to initiate wise, timely and impactful action. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A PowerPoint presentation, a guided contemplative practice designed to offer participants a first-person experience of the “Space Just Before”, and an open Q&A session. RESULTS: Participants are expected to gain greater awareness of their behavioural and cognitive habits, echoing the metaphor articulated by Portia Nelson in Autobiography in Five Short Chapters. The practice of pausing creates an opportunity to interrupt automatic patterns, broaden attentional scope and reconnect with intentional action. This enhanced agency may foster more adaptive, ethically grounded and impactful leadership behaviours. CONCLUSION: The “Space Just Before” is a powerful opportunity to reclaim one’s ability to act with presence and intention. From this expanded awareness, leaders can make conscious, embodied choices and cultivate a form of leadership that is grounded, wise and impactful. Inhabiting the “Space Just Before” represents a meaningful, accessible and evidence-informed resource for leaders seeking to act with clarity, presence and intentionality. By strengthening the capacity for conscious choice, one can cultivate a more grounded, wise, impactful and sustainable form of leadership. TALK TITLE: “DRIVING SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL TRANSFORMATION IN UGANDA THROUGH QUALITY INPUTS, POLICY ALIGNMENT, AND INCLUSIVE AGRIBUSINESS LEADERSHIP” INTRODUCTION: Agriculture remains the backbone of Uganda’s economy, employing more than 70% of the population and contributing significantly to national food security, livelihoods, and export earnings. Despite its importance, the sector continues to face persistent structural and operational challenges that limit productivity and sustainability. These challenges include limited access to certified and affordable agricultural inputs, the widespread circulation of counterfeit and substandard agrochemicals, inadequate and fragmented extension services, and weak alignment between public policy frameworks and private-sector implementation. Smallholder farmers—who constitute the majority of agricultural producers—are disproportionately affected by these constraints, particularly women and youth who often lack access to finance, technology, and markets. In response, sustainable agricultural transformation in Uganda requires a holistic approach that integrates quality input systems, effective regulatory oversight, private-sector leadership, and inclusive agribusiness models. Strengthening collaboration among agribusinesses, regulatory institutions, and farmer organizations is essential to improving productivity, resilience to climate variability, and long-term sector growth. AIM: The aim of this study is to examine how access to quality agricultural inputs, private-sector leadership, and aligned policy collaboration can drive sustainable agricultural transformation in Uganda, with a particular focus on inclusive growth among smallholder farmers, women, and youth. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study adopts a qualitative, case-based approach grounded in professional practice and sector engagement. Data and insights were drawn from over 25 years of experience in agronomy, agribusiness management, and agricultural policy advocacy. Key sources included operational and outreach data from Agrifarm Uganda Ltd, industry coordination and advocacy activities undertaken through CropLife Uganda, and regulatory and policy advisory contributions made through the Agricultural Chemical Board under the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries The analysis also incorporated reviews of farmer training programs, input distribution models, public–private dialogue platforms, and industry-led stakeholder forums. These sources were assessed to determine their effectiveness in improving access to quality inputs, strengthening compliance with agrochemical regulations, reducing the prevalence of counterfeit products, and enhancing farmer productivity and capacity. RESULTS: The findings indicate that improved access to certified seeds, fertilizers, irrigation technologies, and greenhouse systems significantly enhances farm productivity, resilience, and income stability. Strengthened industry coordination resulted in a doubling of CropLife Uganda’s membership within one year, contributing to improved self-regulation and more effective advocacy against counterfeit agrochemicals. Furthermore, structured policy–industry dialogue platforms enhanced trust, regulatory compliance, and predictability within the agricultural sector. CONCLUSION: Sustainable agricultural transformation in Uganda is achievable through coordinated leadership among agribusinesses, regulators, and farmers. Empowering farmers with quality inputs, enforcing regulatory standards, and institutionalizing policy–private sector dialogue are critical to improving food security, increasing incomes, and building long-term resilience within the agricultural sector. KEYWORDS: Agribusiness; Women Empowerment; Export Trade; Value Chains; Sustainable Agriculture BIOGRAPHY: Agnes Mbabazi is a Ugandan agribusiness leader with over 25 years of experience in agriculture, policy advocacy, and farmer empowerment. She is the CEO of Agrifarm Uganda Ltd, Chairperson of CropLife Uganda, and a Board Member of the Agricultural Chemical Board under the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry, and Fisheries. Agnes holds an MBA from Makerere University and a Postgraduate Diploma in Horticulture from the University of Jerusalem, alongside executive training from regional and international institutions. A passionate mentor and advocate for sustainable farming, she has empowered women, youth, and refugee farming communities across Uganda. Thus also serves as Secretary General of the Commonwealth Business Women Africa (CBWA) Uganda Chapter. In 2025, she received the Excellence in Agricultural Innovation Award at the Commonwealth Business Women Africa Summit in Nigeria. TALK TITLE: “THE PURPLE PILL” INTRODUCTION: In today’s high-pressure professional landscape, success is often measured through productivity, revenue, influence, and visible achievements. Yet many high-performing individuals experience burnout, emotional fatigue, and a growing disconnect between their professional success and personal fulfilment. Conventional performance frameworks emphasise output and endurance, while modern wellbeing approaches often lack structure and measurable sustainability. This growing divide leaves leaders trapped between achievement and alignment. The Purple Pill introduces a new paradigm—one that integrates ambition with authenticity, discipline with self-awareness, and performance with emotional and identity alignment. It offers a practical path toward success that does not require sacrificing personal well-being or purpose. AIM: This abstract introduces The Purple Pill and Project 100 as an integrated framework designed to help high-performing individuals balance external success with internal identity, resilience, and self-leadership in a divided modern world. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The Purple Pill functions as the philosophical foundation, while Project 100 provides a structured, results-driven implementation model. The methodology combines identity recalibration, behavioral reprogramming, belief restructuring, and nervous system regulation to create sustainable performance change. Participants move through progressive stages of awareness, accountability, embodiment, and integration, supported by practical frameworks and real-world application tools. This immersive process bridges psychology, leadership development, and business strategy, enabling individuals to redesign their performance patterns and leadership identity without losing authenticity. CONCLUSION: The Purple Pill and Project 100 redefine modern success by removing the false choice between achievement and authenticity. This model represents the future of leadership development—where success is not only measured by external outcomes, but also by internal coherence, resilience, and fulfillment. TALK TITLE: “BRIDGING AGRICULTURE, TRADE, AND WOMEN’S EMPOWERMENT: BUILDING INCLUSIVE EXPORT-LED VALUE CHAINS IN AFRICA” INTRODUCTION: Agriculture plays a central role in Africa’s economic development, employing a significant portion of the population and contributing substantially to national GDPs. Despite its importance, the sector continues to face structural challenges, particularly for smallholder farmers who form the backbone of agricultural production. Women and youth, who represent a large share of this workforce, often encounter barriers such as limited access to finance, modern processing facilities, reliable logistics, and international markets. These constraints reduce their ability to participate meaningfully in global value chains and benefit from export opportunities. In recent years, export-led agribusiness models have emerged as a promising pathway to transform agriculture from subsistence-based production into a commercially viable and globally competitive sector. When combined with integrated logistics and community-centered empowerment initiatives, these models can enhance value addition, improve trade efficiency, and promote inclusive growth. This work explores how purpose-driven leadership and integrated value chain development can bridge the gap between local agricultural production and global markets while advancing women’s and youth empowerment across Africa. AIM: This abstract examines how export-led agribusiness, integrated logistics, and community-centered empowerment models can drive inclusive economic growth, particularly for women and youth in Africa. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study is based on applied leadership experience and operational insights gained from the establishment, growth, and management of Prest Foods Ltd and its affiliated enterprises under Prest Group. Data sources included observational records and operational reports from certified processing facilities, export transactions, logistics operations, farmer engagement programs, and nonprofit empowerment initiatives. The analysis examined activities across multiple stages of the agricultural value chain, including primary production, processing, packaging, logistics, regulatory compliance, and international market access. In addition, qualitative outcomes from community-based programs delivered through the Prest Foods Foundation were reviewed to assess capacity building in climate-smart agriculture, entrepreneurship, branding, and financial literacy among women, youth, widows, and orphans. RESULTS: Prest Foods Ltd operates a certified processing facility handling over 400,000 kilograms of organic produce monthly, exporting to international markets including the United States, Canada, Austria, and Oman under U.S. FDA and REX compliance. Logistics integration through Wajas Logistics Ltd has enhanced cross-border trade efficiency and supply chain reliability. Community empowerment initiatives delivered through the Prest Foods Foundation have equipped women, youth, widows, and orphans with skills in climate-smart agriculture, entrepreneurship, branding, and financial literacy, leading to improved incomes and more sustainable livelihoods. CONCLUSION: The integration of agribusiness, logistics, and social impact initiatives creates a powerful, resilient ecosystem that enables export-led growth while strengthening local communities. By aligning production, processing, compliance, and efficient logistics, these models reduce market barriers and connect smallholder farmers directly to global value chains. Purpose-driven leadership ensures that commercial success is not pursued in isolation, but alongside social responsibility. Within agricultural export ecosystems, this approach enhances income stability, builds skills, and expands opportunities for women and youth. The result is a scalable model that delivers sustainable economic growth, promotes inclusion, and drives long-term social and economic transformation across African communities. TALK TITLE: AUTHENTICITY OVER PRODUCTIVITY: RETHINKING SUCCESS IN HUSTLE CULTURE. INTRODUCTION: Hustle culture prioritises constant productivity, achievement, and performance, often encouraging individuals to equate their self-worth with their accomplishments. Over time, this relentless pursuit of success can disconnect people from their core values, authentic identities, and overall sense of purpose. The pressure to always be available, productive, and successful may contribute to chronic stress, anxiety, emotional exhaustion, and burnout. AIM: Explore authenticity as a protective factor against stress, anxiety, and burnout within hustle culture. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Conceptual keynote drawing on psychological research and clinical psychotherapy practice. RESULTS: Authenticity and value-aligned living are strongly associated with improved psychological well-being, greater life satisfaction, and lower levels of stress and burnout. Individuals who live in accordance with their personal values and authentic selves are more likely to experience a sense of purpose, resilience, and emotional balance, even when facing demanding professional environments. By making decisions that reflect their core beliefs rather than external expectations, they can foster healthier relationships, enhance self-confidence, and maintain long-term motivation. Cultivating authenticity not only protects against emotional exhaustion but also supports sustainable performance, personal growth, and overall mental well-being in both personal and professional life. CONCLUSION: Supporting authenticity may help counter toxic productivity and promote sustainable mental health. I will discuss the importance of how individuals can grow resilience out of trauma through trauma – informed coaching, and integrative, mind body practices. AIM: Using a holistic, strengths-based framework, this work highlights the empowering role of art therapy, trauma-informed yoga, and tai chi in supporting healing and self-reconnection. CONCLUSION: Building resilience after childhood trauma requires approaches that extend beyond traditional interventions. This paper examines women's "invisible wounds" through the lens of Complex Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (C-PTSD), trauma-related internalized beliefs, and the fawning response as adaptive survival strategies. These responses frequently emerge following prolonged exposure to childhood abuse, interpersonal violence, emotional neglect, workplace harassment, institutional discrimination, and other forms of chronic adversity. AIM: Adopting a practitioner-scholar perspective, this conceptual paper synthesizes contemporary empirical evidence, trauma- informed psychological theory, and drawing on clinical experience working with adolescents and adults in Nepal. Particular attention is given to the influence of sociocultural norms and gendered expectations in shaping women's experiences of trauma, coping, and recovery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This paper is based on a comprehensive review of existing literature on women's mental health, trauma, emotional well- being, and gender-responsive care. Relevant research articles, policy documents, and evidence-based frameworks were analyzed to identify the psychological, social, and cultural factors influencing women's trauma experiences. RESULTS: This paper examines how gender-neutral mental health frameworks often overlook the unique ways trauma affects women, leading to misdiagnosis and inadequate care. It proposes a trauma-informed emotional recovery framework built on six key pillars: emotional safety, trust and compassion, empowerment, cultural sensitivity, holistic healing, and psychological resilience. CONCLUSION: Women's emotional well-being is a fundamental human right and a public health priority. This paper highlights the need for trauma-informed, gender-responsive mental health care and calls for collaborative efforts to ensure psychological safety, equitable access to healing, and greater gender equity for stronger, more resilient communities. TALK TITLE: "EFFECTIVENESS OF TRANSACTIONAL ANALYSIS THERAPY ON DEPRESSION AND MARITAL ADJUSTMENT OF COUPLES” INTRODUCTION: Depression and marital conflicts significantly affect the quality of life and family well-being. Transactional Analysis (TA) is a well-established psychological approach that enhances interpersonal relationships, communication, and emotional functioning. This study investigates the effectiveness of TA therapy in improving marital adjustment and reducing depressive symptoms among married couples. AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of Transactional Analysis (TA) Therapy in reducing depression and improving marital adjustment among married couples. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 20 married couples from a psychiatric clinic in Dhaka, Bangladesh, were selected using opportunistic sampling. A repeated-measures design without a control group was employed. Participants underwent 12 TA counseling sessions. Depression was assessed using the Depression Inventory Scale (DIS), and marital adjustment was measured using the Locke Wallace Marital Adjustment Test (LWMAT). Assessments were conducted at pre-test, post-test, and one-month follow-up. RESULTS: The findings demonstrated statistically significant improvements in both depression and marital adjustment scores following TA therapy. Positive effects were maintained at the one-month follow-up, indicating sustained therapeutic benefits. CONCLUSION: Transactional Analysis Therapy appears to be an effective intervention for reducing depression and enhancing marital adjustment among married couples. Further studies with larger, more diverse samples and randomized controlled designs are recommended to strengthen the evidence. Keywords: Transactional Analysis, Depression, Marital adjustment, Couple Counselling. Drawing from lived experience and original research, this keynote introduces The Great Shedding™, a structural workforce shift impacting experienced professionals displaced amid organizational redesign, automation, and AI-driven transformation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This work is grounded in qualitative insights, lived experience following a 30-year corporate career, and analysis of workforce trends, including over 1.2 million U.S. job cuts in 2025. The methodology integrates narrative case studies, composite profiles, and a five-phase identity reinvention model developed through practitioner-based research and executive coaching practice. RESULTS: Findings reveal that traditional outplacement models inadequately address the psychological and identity-based dimensions of career disruption. Participants experience what is defined as the Identity Void, a gap between professional identity loss and redefinition. The five-phase model—Disruption, Disillusion, Detachment, Discovery, and Design—provides a structured pathway for navigating this transition and rebuilding professional agency. CONCLUSION: Identity reinvention is not a linear career exercise but an internal transformation process. By integrating emotional mastery, identity reconstruction, and self-leadership, individuals can reclaim agency and redefine success on their own terms. This work reframes displacement from loss to opportunity for intentional reinvention. Rather than directing blame at individuals, I began writing letters to my children. Those letters became a disciplined method of reflection, allowing me to process experience while remaining anchored to integrity. What began as personal narrative evolved into structured inquiry AIM: To examine how authentic storytelling can evolve into strategic leadership, enabling women to build networks of allies, influence institutions, and drive purpose-led reform. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Through continued writing, pattern recognition, and engagement with others navigating similar institutional systems, I shifted from examining individual decisions to analyzing system design. Lived experience was translated into structured narrative analysis, cross-case pattern mapping, and strategic alliance-building with advocates, policymakers, and reform leaders. Storytelling became not an emotional outlet, but a deliberate method of influence and collaboration. RESULTS: When authentic narrative is paired with systems literacy, it generates credibility and attracts cross-disciplinary allies. Consistent storytelling grounded in clarity and integrity opens constructive dialogue within institutions. This approach has supported conversations around accountability, implementation gaps, and child-centered reform within complex systems. CONCLUSION: Purpose-driven leadership does not require formal authority; it requires clarity of mission and disciplined use of voice. By transforming lived experience into structured insight, women can build alliances that influence institutional change. Authentic storytelling, when aligned with strategy, becomes a catalyst not only for healing, but for measurable reform. TALK TITLE: ACHIEVING EXCELLENCE: WHY PROGRESS DOESN’T EQUAL PERFECTION INTRODUCTION: Excellence in the workplace is best understood as an ongoing practice rather than a final achievement. It is sustained through reliable performance, solution‑oriented thinking, transparent communication, personal accountability, and mutual respect. When employees adopt these principles, they elevate both their own contributions and the broader team’s effectiveness. At the organizational level, excellence is reinforced by a clear vision, continuous learning opportunities, consistent measurement of progress, and meaningful employee engagement. Together, these individual behaviors and structural supports create a culture where progress is valued over perfection and long‑term growth becomes possible. AIM: The aim is to capture the central message that excellence is a continuous mindset built through daily behaviors and supported by organizational systems, not a pursuit of flawlessness. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The aim is to capture the central message that excellence is a continuous mindset built through daily behaviors and supported by organizational systems, not a pursuit of flawlessness. RESULTS: Workplace excellence is built through consistent performance, accountability, clear communication, and a solution-oriented mindset. Organizations sustain excellence by setting clear expectations, supporting employee growth, measuring performance, and fostering an empowering workplace culture. CONCLUSION: Excellence happens when people choose to show up with intention every day. It’s built through reliability, honest communication, accountability, and respect—habits that strengthen teams and elevate results. Organizations that pair these habits with clear goals, learning‑driven cultures, and consistent measurement create workplaces where progress is celebrated and perfection is never the expectation. Excellence becomes a shared journey, not a destination. TALK TITLE: THE HIDDEN STRENGTHS OF NEURODIVERSITY IN LEADERSHIP INTRODUCTION: Millions of neurodivergent individuals including those with ADHD, autism, dyslexia, and other cognitive differences possess extraordinary strengths that remain overlooked because educational systems and workplaces continue to emphasize conformity over individuality. As organizations seek innovation in an increasingly complex world, recognizing and nurturing neurodiverse talent has become both a social responsibility and a strategic advantage. AIM: This keynote aims to challenge conventional perspectives on leadership by demonstrating how neurodiversity fuels creativity, innovation, systems thinking, resilience, and authentic leadership. It encourages participants to shift from asking 'How do we help people fit in?' to 'What unique strengths can we help them develop? MATERIALS AND METHODS: The presentation combines personal lived experience as an ADHD entrepreneur, software engineer, and parent of a child with ADHD, together with current research, practical examples, and interactive audience reflection. Visual storytelling and real-world leadership examples illustrate how inclusive environments unlock exceptional human potential. RESULTS: Participants will gain a deeper understanding of neurodiversity beyond deficits and discover how many leadership qualities including creative problem solving, pattern recognition, resilience, hyperfocus, empathy, and original thinking are often found within neurodivergent individuals. The session explores the hidden costs of masking, the importance of psychological safety, and practical ways educators, employers, healthcare professionals, and leaders can cultivate environments where diverse minds thrive. By embracing authenticity and creating cultures of belonging, organizations can improve innovation, engagement, and long-term success. CONCLUSION: The future belongs to leaders with open minds and open hearts. Unlocking the strengths of neurodiversity requires curiosity, compassion, and a commitment to creating environments where differences are recognized as valuable assets rather than obstacles. By shifting our perspective from fixing people to empowering them, we create stronger individuals, healthier organizations, and a more innovative society. Survivors often face challenges such as survivor's guilt, fear of change, and identity struggles. This presentation explores how resilience, storytelling, and self-reflection can transform adversity into empowerment while encouraging healing and personal growth. AIM: To explore the impact of childhood trauma and surviving cancer on personal identity and emotional well-being, and to demonstrate how storytelling and creative expression can foster resilience, healing, and hope for others facing similar life challenges. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This presentation is based on the author's lived experiences as a childhood trauma survivor and young cancer survivor, combined with reflective storytelling and creative writing. Insights are drawn from personal memoir development, published literary works, public speaking engagements, and observations of resilience through creative expression and community engagement. RESULTS: The journey demonstrates that acknowledging trauma and embracing vulnerability can lead to personal growth and emotional healing. Storytelling emerged as a powerful therapeutic tool, helping transform survivor's guilt into purpose while inspiring others to confront fear, embrace change, and build resilience. Creative works such as children's literature and memoir writing further reinforce messages of hope, courage, and recovery. CONCLUSION: Healing is a lifelong process that requires courage, self-compassion, and the willingness to share one's story. By transforming painful experiences into meaningful narratives, individuals can empower themselves and others, creating greater awareness of trauma-informed healing and the strength found in resilience. Theme: ‘’From Representation to Reinvention: Transforming Women's Power and Redefining Leadership for the Future “ Aim: The purpose of the presentation is to critically analyze the limitations of representation-driven women's empowerment; introduce an intersectional approach to leadership and institutionalized equity; share my original REVISE Leadership Framework and provide practical recommendations for transformation. Introduction: In the conversations about women's leadership all around the world, much of the attention has been devoted to growing representation. However, merely having access to a leadership role does not necessarily mean having influence, power or the ability to change organizational priorities. The persistent gender gaps in economic, political, academic and civic leadership reveal that, besides the question of whether women have access to the existing systems, there is an equally important question about whether the existing system is still too narrowly and hierarchically defined by the same historical gender power dynamics. This keynote challenges the concept of empowerment through redefining it as agency-building, solidarity and decision-shaping process. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This 30-minute evidence-based keynote uses a conceptual synthesis of global gender gap reports, feminist and inclusive leadership literature, organizational studies and cross-sector examples. Infographics, flowcharts, an institutional barriers 'iceberg', a leadership evolution timeline and reflective questions will be employed to convert theory into practice-friendly language in the international conference setting. The presentation is a scholarly keynote rather than an empirical research paper. A separate systematic literature review was conducted before working the presentation the for conference. RESULTS: The implementation of structured project management approaches, cross-functional collaboration, and technology-driven solutions has contributed to improved project efficiency, stronger stakeholder engagement, enhanced operational performance, and successful delivery of complex technical initiatives. CONCLUSION: Any real revision of women's leadership requires individual agency to be matched with institutional responsibility. Women should not have to be better adapted to the inherited model of authority; organizations should revise values, structure and behavior underlying the existing leadership recognition and reward system. The future of the leadership is not just female; it is plural, ethical and transformative. The audience will be invited to choose one hidden barrier to their success, one practice to revise and one action that can be done in 90 days. Talk Title: “Born Leaders. Trained out of it.” Aim: This keynote aims to reframe the conversation around women and leadership — from development and deficit to preservation and protection. It will equip attendees with a new lens through which to understand their own leadership journey, identify the interference patterns that accumulated as a response to formal leadership structures, and reconnect with the natural leadership instincts that were always present. Introduction: For decades, the leadership industry has asked a single question: "How do we develop more women leaders?" This question, while well-intentioned, contains a flawed assumption — that women arrive at leadership incomplete. Neuroscience, behavioural research and real-world observation tell a different story. Women demonstrate sophisticated leadership instincts long before they hold a formal title, instincts that are neurologically grounded and empirically evidenced. Yet something changes when women enter formal leadership structures. The very qualities that made them powerful become liabilities in systems designed around a different model. Women are not failing to rise. They are being trained out of the very thing that made them powerful in the first place. MATERIALS AND METHODS: For this key note I will work from prepared slides and engage the thought process of the audience with a few questions. RESULTS: Drawing on neuroscience research including Simon Baron-Cohen's work on empathy and Zenger and Folkman's longitudinal study of 16,000 leaders, this keynote demonstrates that women's leadership capabilities are not absent — they are obscured. The interference patterns that develop in response to formal leadership structures — perfectionism, people-pleasing, fear of losing control, shame and self-doubt — are adaptive strategies, not character flaws. The Inhabit Framework, introduced in this session, maps these patterns to the leadership tools they block, offering a practical model for removing interference and reclaiming already-present capability. The discussion reframes "women's leadership development" as an inside-out process of returning to self, rather than an outside-in process of acquiring more. CONCLUSION: Women are natural leaders. Neuroscience, data, and everyday experience show that the issue has never been capability—it has been systems that suppress natural leadership instincts. Rather than treating women's leadership as something to develop, we should preserve and empower what already exists. Attendees will leave with a new perspective on their leadership and practical tools to lead more authentically—not by becoming someone new, but by returning to who they already are. KEYWORDS: Women in leadership, leadership development, neuroscience of leadership, born to lead, leadership interference patterns, the Inhabit Framework, self-leadership, women's leadership preservation, inside-out leadership, leadership identity BIOGRAPHY: Rebecca Doyle is a leadership coach, facilitator, author and speaker with over two decades of experience across Australia and beyond. Talk Title: “Wired and Tired: Why Your Nervous System Holds The Key To Sleep” AIM: To demonstrate that insomnia is not a sleep problem; it’s a nervous system regulation issue, and to give the audience practical internal tools to restore natural sleep. INTRODUCTION: I’ve run 12 marathons in 12 years, but I started running at three—escaping danger after homeless men broke into our home. For nearly 70 years, my nervous system never felt safe enough to rest, and I slept just 2–3 hours a night. Everything changed when I learned that the body holds onto trauma long after the mind has moved on. Today, at 75, I sleep through the night, train in jujitsu, run, and have more energy than I ever imagined. If a nervous system shaped over 70 years can change, anyone's can. I’ve seen this transformation in my clients too—including an executive who stopped waking at 2 a.m. every night after decades of disrupted sleep. When the body feels safe, rest, recovery, and performance become possible. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This keynote blends neuroscience, subconscious reprogramming, and live audience experience. Participants will: -Experience interactive exercises that demonstrate how thoughts directly influence physiological state -Learn why traditional sleep strategies often fail high performers -Understand how subconscious patterns keep the body in a state of alertness -Apply simple, internal shifts that allow the nervous system to transition into rest RESULTS: Attendees will leave with: A clear understanding of why they feel ‘wired and tired.’ The ability to recognize and interrupt nighttime overactivation. - Practical tools to calm the nervous system in real time A new relationship with sleep, one that is internal, sustainable, and not dependent on external routines alone. CONCLUSION: IInsomnia is not simply the inability to sleep; it is the inability for the body to feel safe enough to let go, insight. When the nervous system shifts, sleep follows. Whether falling asleep or waking in the middle of the night, the most powerful intervention is not effort; it is regulation. This talk gives the audience more than insight. It gives them the ability to return their body to calm, to quiet the mind, and to access the deep rest required for clarity, recovery, and high-level performance. KEYWORDS: Nervous system, insomnia, sleep, stress, neuroscience, subconscious patterns, anxiety, burnout, resilience, recovery, self- regulation, high performance, wellbeing, transformation. INTRODUCTION \ BACKGROUND: As female leaders, we have collectively encountered the distinctive challenge of managing our professional teams with greater efficacy than our familial relationships. Upon examining the term "leader," one discovers a multitude of interpretations. According to the Cambridge Dictionary, a leader is defined as "a person in control of a group, country, or situation." This raises the question of why gender should exert an influence on our leadership capabilities. Furthermore, in what ways do our varied roles shape our effectiveness in leadership positions? AIM / OBJECTIVE: This discussion aims to explore the various factors that may be perceived as obstacles for women in leadership roles. It is imperative that we initiate a constructive dialogue. Is the impediment to ascending to higher positions attributable to gender, or is it a consequence of the additional obligations that we, as female leaders, bear? Your insights and lived experiences are crucial to this discourse. MATERIALS AND METHODS BY APPROACH: In this keynote presentation, I will utilize PowerPoint as a visual aid and actively engage the audience through thought-provoking questions. RESULTS / DISCUSSION: The essence of effective leadership transcends the simplistic notion of being in control, as articulated by the Cambridge Dictionary; irrespective of gender, a leader is perceived as the custodian of revenue generation in the eyes of shareholders. Nevertheless, for female leaders, the role extends beyond mere revenue generation; we concurrently assume multiple responsibilities across various domains. These roles include but are not limited to, those of a mother, spouse, daughter, daughter-in-law, sister, grandmother, caregiver, chauffeur, chef, and housekeeper. Our attempts to excel in each of these multifaceted roles can lead to an imbalance, resulting in burnout, distraction, and confusion; these disruptive emotions ultimately reflect on our professional performance. Consequently, the act of juggling these diverse responsibilities contributes to a perception that undermines our capacity to manage more significant roles within the corporate sphere. CONCLUSION / SUMMARY: To enhance our prospects of being regarded for leadership positions, it is essential that we cultivate the ability to delegate and effectively manage our personal responsibilities. By relinquishing or adequately managing these supplementary roles, we can concentrate on and showcase our distinctive perspectives and competencies, thereby empowering ourselves throughout our leadership journey. Cllr Fatima Zaman Abstract: In evaluating contemporary trauma-informed and person- centered approaches, the article explores the role of empathy, collaboration, and empowerment in clinical practice. These approaches are further contextualized through detailed case studies and intervention strategies that highlight the tangible benefits of treating patients as whole persons rather than as diagnostic categories. Ultimately, this article advocates for a reimagined psychiatric paradigm that prioritizes healing relationships, long-term wellness, and systemic transformation in mental health services. She is recognized as an Amazon bestselling author for her volumes “Afghanistan: A Memoir from Brooklyn to Kabul,” parts one and two, and she serves as an international speaker on the subject of Afghan cultural studies. In response to the Soviet invasion and subsequent occupation, she shifted her focus to humanitarian efforts, assuming the role of Director at the Afghanistan Foundation. While traversing the Hindu Kush Mountains alongside Afghan resistance fighters, she facilitated the distribution of vegetable seeds for agricultural cultivation, which were sourced from the Girl Scouts of America. Additionally, she provided sewing kits gathered by American elementary school students for war widows residing in refugee camps in Pakistan, thereby addressing issues of idleness and mental health. Furthermore, she transported RH negative blood to the Afghan Women’s Hospital in Peshawar, Pakistan, for women experiencing spontaneous abortions, as well as powdered milk for infants in critical need. Materials and Methods: Cat Parenti consistently engaged with Afghan communities at the grassroots level. Her inaugural entrepreneurial venture focused on Afghan handicrafts, wherein she employed local male tailors and female embroiderers, offering them a living wage and marketing their artisanal products in New York City. Her subsequent enterprise involved the procurement of antique silver tribal jewelry and commissioning Afghan artisans to replicate these ancient designs for the American consumer market, with sales directed towards museum shops along the eastern seaboard of the United States. Confronted with the severe restrictions imposed on women by the Taliban, Cat Parenti reverted to the traditional practice of women undertaking embroidery work within their domestic spaces. She established the Afghan Women’s Empowerment Program (AWEP), encapsulated by the motto “A Hand Up Not a Hand Out,” which seeks to empower young widows through the provision of housing, sustenance, and resources to engage in their handicrafts. The resulting products, which include pillow covers, dresses, and long scarves, are marketed internationally, thus alleviating the necessity for these women to resort to begging on the streets with their children. This initiative enables them to attain self-sufficiency as heads of their households. The overarching objective of AWEP is to expand the program's reach to encompass women with physical disabilities. TALK TITLE: THE HIDDEN, UNACCOUNTED, AND UNSEEN TAX OF FEMALE ENTREPRENEURSHIP INTRODUCTION \ BACKGROUND: Female entrepreneurs face unique challenges that extend beyond conventional business risks. While funding gaps, limited networks, and discrimination are widely recognized, there exists a deeper layer of “hidden taxes” that silently erode potential. These unseen barriers—such as self-doubt, perfectionism, and fear of technology—add an invisible cost that limits growth, equity, and sustainability in women-led ventures. AIM / OBJECTIVE: To explore both the known and lesser-known “taxes” on female entrepreneurship, highlight their impact on venture performance and personal wellbeing, and propose strategies to recognize, reduce, and overcome these barriers. MATERIALS AND METHODS BY APPROACH: The talk draws upon: Case Studies of women entrepreneurs across different geographies. Economic and Social Research on gender equity in entrepreneurship. Personal Narratives reflecting real-world experiences with visible and invisible barriers. Comparative Analysis of structural vs. psychological taxes influencing female entrepreneurship. RESULTS / DISCUSSION: Known Taxes Identified: Barriers to funding, networking limitations, work-life imbalance, discrimination and bias, and lower business valuations. Less-Known Taxes Revealed: Low self-worth, self-doubt, constant need for validation, perfectionism, limited access/fear of technology, and the “hobbification” of women’s businesses (ventures being treated as hobbies rather than serious enterprises). These taxes reduce ROI, restrict access to opportunities, slow growth, and limit women’s participation in emerging venture trends. CONCLUSION / SUMMARY: Female Entrepreneurship, Hidden Taxes, Gender Equity, Funding Barriers, Self-Doubt, Perfectionism, Venture Growth, Technology Adoption KEYWORDS: Play, Creative Play, Well-Being, Storytelling, Story, Empathy, Shared Humanity, One Human FAMILY, Social Justice, Ecological Justice, Playful Activities, Conservation, clean-water, Cognitive Development, Emotional Development, books, music, Musical Play, songs, dissertation. TALK TITLE: SHE IS THE ENGINE: EMPOWERING THE NEXT GENERATION OF FEMALE ENTREPRENEURS THROUGH THE R.E.A.L. ENGINETM BLUEPRINT FOR INCLUSIVE GROWTH. INTRODUCTION: From Cameroon’s informal markets to emerging tech hubs across the Global South, women sustain families, communities, and economies. Yet their contributions remain undervalued, underfunded, and constrained by structural barriers, including limited access to finance, mentorship, and policy influence. Closing the gender gap could add USD 12 trillion to global GDP by 2025 (McKinsey, 2020), yet women own only one-third of businesses and receive less than 2% of venture capital funding (Pitch Book & WEF, 2023).This work asks: What happens when we stop overlooking women as contributors and build frameworks that enable them to lead? AIM / OBJECTIVE: Female entrepreneurs remain both an underutilized resource and a catalytic force for inclusive, sustainable growth. This presentation examine show the R.E.A.L. Engine™ Framework (Resilience, Education, Actionable Skills, and Leadership) can move women from peripheral participation to economic leadership, driving growth and creating lasting legacies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The R.E.A.L. Engine™ Framework, developed through the Ladies Arise and Connect initiative, integrates structured literacy for dyslexia, resilience training, opportunity-recognition modules, and mentorship. Data from n=120 girls aged 14–24 in five semi-urban communities were collected using the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), a validated literacy assessment, community mapping, surveys, and case studies. Findings highlight that dyslexic individuals often excel in creativity, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills embedded in the model to promote inclusive innovation. RESULTS / DISCUSSION: Participants receiving targeted education, mentorship, and leadership opportunities recorded a 26% average increase in opportunity recognition scores and improved business sustainability measures over six months. Neurodiverse-inclusive ecosystems, particularly those embracing dyslexia, demonstrated higher innovation capacity. Case studies from Cameroon and Latin America showed that inclusive skill-building and leadership accelerators foster enterprise creation, economic mobility, and intergenerational wealth transfer. TALK TITLE: THE ROLE OF TRUST-BASED SCANDINAVIAN MANAGEMENT MODEL FOR THE SUSTAINABLE FUTURE Abstract: Aim: This presentation aims to explore how the Scandinavian management style, rooted in trust, inclusivity, and flat organizational structures, contributes to organizational sustainability and societal well-being. It also highlights practical leadership strategies that can be applied in different parts of the world. Introduction: Scandinavian countries are often seen as global leaders in sustainability and well-being and consistently ranked among the world’s most sustainable and happiest societies. One of the factors behindthis success is their uniquemanagement philosophy, which emphasizes trust, autonomy, and inclusivity. This model contrasts sharply with hierarchical and control- based systems. Materials and Methods: My reflections are based on a qualitative review of Scandinavian organizational practices. It combines leadership theories, academic literature on sustainable leadership, and sustainability models. I make use of examples from both publicand private organizations in Norway, personal experiences and employee feedback data to understand how trust- based management affects performance and well-being. Results: Findings indicate that trust-based leadership contributes to better employee satisfaction, reduced turnover, and stronger commitment to sustainability goals. Giving employees more freedom to make decisions and promoting open communication leads to more innovation, resilience and responsibility. Policies that support work-life balance also help improve long-term well-being, productivity and health. Conclusion: The Scandinavian model offers a practical and effective way to lead sustainably. By building trust, collaboration and inclusivity into the workplace culture, leaders can improve both results and purpose. The principles of this model can be adapted to fit differentcultures and industries around the world. Keywords: Scandinavian Management • Trust-Based Leadership • Sustainability • Organizational Culture• Employee Empowerment• Decentralized Decision-Making • Work-Life Balance Biography: Katerina von Baudissin was born on September 28, 1984. Early Career: The Foundation of My Work I started my career in Kentucky state government with a degree in Agribusiness and an MBA. My first job was at the Board of Hairdressers, where I was hired as a data entry operator. Although it was a junior role, it was an invaluable learning experience. I worked alongside experts who mentored me and taught me the practical applications of the knowledge I gained in school. During those first few years, I focused on building my skills and understanding the dynamics of Kentucky state government. After I was hired at the Ky Cabinet for Human Resources (CHFS) as an accountant and then a health planner, I often found myself working late, eager to absorb as much as I could. Growth and Transition: Expanding My Horizons After several years of gaining hands-on experience, I realized that I wanted to take on more responsibilities and challenge myself. In May 1995, I took on a new role as Health Planner at CHFS. This was a turning point in my career. I was responsible for answering inquiries, various healthcare topics and putting on town forums across the state, which tested my leadership abilities and sharpened my problem-solving skills. One of my proudest moments during this period was when I successfully helped run unscrupulous insurance companies out of the state, thus having healthcare issues such as pregnancy and/or other pre-existing conditions. Leadership Roles: Taking Charge and Making an Impact By 1995, I was ready for a leadership role. I became the lead analyst over the Health and Family Service Cabinet at the Kentucky Legislative Research Commission, where I was responsible for overseeing the $13 billion health and family services budget. I became a licensed insurance agent in 2018, and have sold home, Medicare and Life agent all over the USA. One of my key accomplishments in this role was to gain the trust of all staff which is a major achievement as a leader, such as improving outcomes, launching a new program, or leading team on budget analysts. This success not only demonstrated my leadership abilities but also reaffirmed my passion for the work I do. Current Role and Future Aspirations: Continuing the Journey Today, I am a Licensed Insurance agent at The Murray Group, where I continue to grow and evolve as a professional. I am proud of the journey I’ve taken and the skills I’ve acquired, but I know that there is always more to learn and new challenges to face. My current role involves selling various insurance products, and I am excited about the opportunity to continue making an impact. Looking forward, I am focused on continuing my education and/or maintain my skills, taking on larger projects, or mentoring . I am committed to continuous professional development and staying ahead of industry trends to ensure that I continue to offer value to my company and colleagues. Conclusion: A Lifelong Commitment to Growth Reflecting on my career so far, I am grateful for every experience and challenge that has helped me grow. From my early days as an eager learner to my current role as a top legislative analyst and then a licensed insurance agent, I’ve learned that success comes from a combination of passion, hard work, and the willingness to adapt. My journey is far from over, and I look forward to continuing my professional growth and contributing to the future success of my field.
